Steel, with an intermediate carbon content, combined strength and toughness, but it was so expensive that it was used mainly for tools, springs and weapons.

In 1856, the English inventor Henry Bessemer announced a method that changed this situation. He blew air through molten pig iron in a large vessel known as a converter. The oxygen in the air reacted with carbon and silicon in the metal, and these reactions released so much heat that the iron stayed liquid without any additional fuel. In about twenty minutes, several tonnes of iron could be converted into steel.

The process was not an immediate success. Early Bessemer steel was often brittle, because the method did not remove phosphorus and left too much oxygen in the metal. The problems were solved by others: adding manganese improved quality, and in the late 1870s Sidney Gilchrist Thomas introduced a basic lining that captured phosphorus. With cheap steel available, railways, ships and skyscrapers could be built on a new scale. The Bessemer converter has long disappeared, but its central idea survives in modern oxygen steelmaking.

questions.q: According to the passage, before Bessemer's invention, steel was used mainly for tools and weapons because ----.
options: it was more brittle than cast iron
it contained no carbon
it could be produced only in blast furnaces, which were rare at the time
it was too costly for large-scale use
it was weaker than wrought iron and could not be used for railways
questions.explain: Metin 'it was so expensive that it was used mainly for tools' diyor. Şık 'expensive' yerine 'too costly for large-scale use' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Bessemer'den önce çelik neden esas olarak alet ve silahlarda kullanılıyordu? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Çelik o kadar pahalıydı ki esas olarak alet, yay ve silahlarda kullanıldı.'
why: Kırılgan olan dökme demirdi; çelik mukavemet ve tokluğu birleştiriyordu.
Metinle çelişiyor: çeliğin karbon içeriği orta düzeyde.
Yüksek fırında dökme demir üretiliyordu; çelik değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: çelik güçlü ve tok bir malzeme.
questions.tip: 'So ... that' kalıbı sebep-sonuç verir; 'so' ile 'that' arasındaki kelime sebebi söyler.

questions.q: It can be understood from the passage that the Bessemer process did not need additional fuel because ----.
options: the converter was heated by electricity supplied from an external source
pig iron melts at room temperature
the chemical reactions inside the vessel released sufficient heat
manganese supplied extra heat
the whole process took only about twenty minutes, so the metal had no time to cool
questions.explain: Metin oksijenin karbon ve silisyumla tepkimesinin 'released so much heat' olduğunu söylüyor. Şık 'so much heat' yerine 'sufficient heat' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Bessemer süreci neden ek yakıt gerektirmiyordu? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Bu tepkimeler o kadar ısı açığa çıkardı ki demir ek yakıt olmadan sıvı kaldı.'
why: Metinde dış elektrik kaynağından söz edilmiyor.
Mantıksız ve metinde yok: pik demir oda sıcaklığında erimez.
Manganez sonradan kaliteyi artırmak için eklendi; ısı için değil.
Süre 20 dakika ama sebep bu değil; ısıyı tepkimeler sağlıyor.
questions.tip: Sebep sorusunda doğru bilgi taşıyan ama sebep olmayan şıklara dikkat; 'because' ile bağlanan cümleyi kontrol et.

questions.q: The author mentions Sidney Gilchrist Thomas in order to ----.
options: claim that he invented the converter several years before Bessemer announced his method
argue that phosphorus, when captured by a basic lining, actually improves steel quality
explain why the converter disappeared
illustrate that others had to refine the method before it fully succeeded
suggest that Bessemer's idea was useless
questions.explain: Metin 'The problems were solved by others' deyip Thomas'ı örnek veriyor. Şık bunu 'others had to refine the method before it fully succeeded' diye özetliyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazar Sidney Gilchrist Thomas'tan neden söz ediyor? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Sorunları başkaları çözdü... Thomas fosforu tutan bazik bir astar getirdi.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: Thomas astarı Bessemer'den yıllar sonra, 1870'lerde getirdi.
Metinle çelişiyor: fosfor çeliği kırılganlaştırıyordu; astar onu tutup sorunu çözdü.
Konvertörün kaybolması son cümlede; Thomas ile ilgisi yok.
Yazar fikrin işe yaramadığını söylemiyor; ana fikir bugün de yaşıyor.
questions.tip: 'Mentions X in order to' sorusunda X'ten hemen önceki genel cümleyi bul; X o cümlenin örneğidir.

title: Cleaning the Exhaust
text:
A petrol engine does not burn its fuel perfectly. Along with carbon dioxide and water, its exhaust contains carbon monoxide, unburnt hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides, all of which harm human health and contribute to smog. Since the 1970s, stricter air-quality laws in many countries have made it necessary to remove most of these pollutants before they leave the tailpipe.

The device that does this is the catalytic converter. Inside a metal case is a ceramic block with thousands of narrow channels, which give it an enormous surface area. The walls of these channels are coated with tiny amounts of precious metals, mainly platinum, palladium and rhodium. These metals act as catalysts: they speed up chemical reactions without being consumed themselves. Carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons are oxidised to carbon dioxide and water, while nitrogen oxides are reduced to harmless nitrogen.

For all three reactions to work efficiently at once, the engine must run with a very precise ratio of air to fuel. An oxygen sensor in the exhaust continuously sends information to the engine's computer, which adjusts the fuel supply many times per second. The converter also works poorly until it is hot, so a large share of emissions from a modern car occur in the first minutes after a cold start. Because the precious metals are valuable, catalytic converters have unfortunately become a frequent target of thieves.

questions.q: According to the passage, the precious metals in a catalytic converter ----.
options: are consumed after each journey
convert carbon dioxide back into carbon monoxide and unburnt hydrocarbons
accelerate reactions without being used up
cool the exhaust gases
replace the need for an oxygen sensor and an engine computer in modern cars
questions.explain: Metin 'speed up chemical reactions without being consumed themselves' diyor. Şık 'speed up' yerine 'accelerate', 'consumed' yerine 'used up' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Katalitik konvertördeki değerli metaller ne yapar? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Bu metaller katalizördür: kendileri tükenmeden kimyasal tepkimeleri hızlandırırlar.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: katalizörler tükenmez.
Yönü ters çeviriyor: CO, CO2'ye dönüşür; tersi değil.
Metinde egzozu soğuttukları yazmıyor; tersine konvertör sıcakken iyi çalışır.
Metinle çelişiyor: oksijen sensörü ve bilgisayar hâlâ gerekli.
questions.tip: Metinde iki nokta üst üste (:) bir tanım verir; tanım sorusunda o kısmı oku.

questions.q: The oxygen sensor mentioned in the passage is needed in order to ----.
options: measure how much platinum and palladium remain in the converter after each trip
heat the converter quickly after a cold start so that it begins to work sooner
detect thieves
help keep the air-to-fuel ratio within a narrow range
increase the production of nitrogen oxides
questions.explain: Üç tepkime için 'very precise ratio of air to fuel' gerekiyor ve sensör bunun ayarlanmasına yardım ediyor. Şık bunu 'keep the air-to-fuel ratio within a narrow range' ile söylüyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Oksijen sensörü neden gerekli? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Motor çok hassas bir hava-yakıt oranıyla çalışmalı; sensör bilgisayara bilgi gönderir, bilgisayar yakıtı ayarlar.'
why: Sensör egzozdaki oksijeni ölçer; metal miktarını değil.
Sensör ısıtma yapmaz; soğuk çalışma ayrı bir bilgi.
Hırsızlık son cümlede ayrı bir konu; sensörle ilgisi yok.
Metinle çelişiyor: amaç azot oksitlerini azaltmak.
questions.tip: 'In order to' sorusunda cihazın bilgi gönderdiği yeri ve oradaki amacı takip et.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that short car trips from a cold start ----.
options: produce no pollutants at all, since the engine has not yet reached full power
make the converter work most efficiently because the engine is still cool
produce relatively high emissions per kilometre
damage the ceramic block
require no fuel adjustment
questions.explain: Emisyonun çoğu ilk dakikalarda oluyorsa, kısa yolculukta her kilometreye düşen kirlilik yüksek olur. Şık bunu 'relatively high emissions per kilometre' diye çıkarıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Soğuk çalıştırmayla yapılan kısa yolculuklar için ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Konvertör ısınana kadar kötü çalışır; emisyonların büyük kısmı soğuk çalıştırmadan sonraki ilk dakikalarda olur.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: ilk dakikalarda emisyon en yüksek.
Metinle çelişiyor: konvertör sıcakken iyi çalışır, soğukken kötü.
Seramik bloğa zarar verildiği metinde yok.
Metinle çelişiyor: yakıt saniyede birçok kez ayarlanıyor.
questions.tip: Çıkarım sorusunda metindeki bilgiyi soruya uygula: 'ilk dakikalar kirli' ise 'kısa yolculuk' daha kirli olur.

title: Forecasting with Machines
text:
For more than half a century, weather forecasts have been produced by numerical models. These programs divide the atmosphere into millions of boxes and solve the physical equations of fluid motion, heat and moisture for each one. They are remarkably skilful, but they require some of the most powerful supercomputers in the world, and a single global forecast can take hours of computing time.

In the past few years, a different approach has emerged. Technology companies and research centres have trained machine-learning models on decades of past weather data. Instead of solving physical equations, these models learn statistical patterns that link the state of the atmosphere at one moment to its state a few hours later. Once trained, they can produce a ten-day global forecast in about a minute on a single processor, and in several tests their accuracy has matched or exceeded that of leading traditional models for many variables.

Meteorologists, however, are not ready to abandon physics. Machine-learning models are trained on data that were themselves created with the help of traditional models, so they still depend on them. They may also perform poorly for rare and extreme events, which by definition appear infrequently in the training data. Many experts therefore expect a hybrid future, in which physical models and machine learning work together, each compensating for the other's weaknesses.

questions.q: According to the passage, a major advantage of machine-learning forecasts is that they ----.
options: solve the physical equations of fluid motion more precisely than traditional models do
do not require any past data
always predict extreme events accurately
have already replaced traditional models completely in most weather centres
take far less time and far less computing power to produce
questions.explain: Geleneksel model süper bilgisayarda saatler sürerken yenisi 'about a minute on a single processor' ile çalışıyor. Şık bunu 'far less time and far less computing power' diye veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Makine öğrenmesi tahminlerinin büyük avantajı ne? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Eğitildikten sonra tek bir işlemcide yaklaşık bir dakikada on günlük küresel tahmin üretebilir.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: bu modeller fizik denklemi çözmez.
Metinle çelişiyor: onlarca yıllık geçmiş veriyle eğitiliyorlar.
Metinle çelişiyor: aşırı olaylarda kötü olabilirler; 'always' aşırı.
Metinle çelişiyor: meteorologlar fiziği bırakmaya hazır değil.
questions.tip: Avantaj sorusunda eski ve yeni yöntemin rakamlarını (saatler / bir dakika) karşılaştır.

questions.q: Meteorologists are reluctant to abandon physical models partly because ----.
options: physical models are cheaper to run
machine-learning models are never accurate for ordinary variables such as temperature
rare and extreme events appear far too frequently in the data used for training
supercomputers are no longer available
the newer models depend on data generated partly by the older ones
questions.explain: Metin 'trained on data that were themselves created with the help of traditional models' diyor. Şık 'created with the help of' yerine 'generated partly by the older ones' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Meteorologlar fiziksel modelleri neden bırakmak istemiyor? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Makine öğrenmesi modelleri geleneksel modellerin yardımıyla oluşturulan verilerle eğitiliyor, yani onlara bağımlı.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: fiziksel modeller pahalı süper bilgisayar ister.
Metinle çelişiyor: yeni modeller birçok değişkende eskileri yakaladı; 'never' yanlış.
Ters bilgi: aşırı olaylar verilerde nadir görülür, sık değil.
Süper bilgisayarların ortadan kalktığı metinde yok.
questions.tip: 'Partly because' sorusunda paragraf birden çok sebep verir; şıklardan birini metinde birebir bul.

questions.q: The passage suggests that the future of weather forecasting will most likely ----.
options: rely only on machine learning once enough past data has been collected
return to forecasts made without computers
combine physical and machine-learning methods
ignore extreme weather events
depend on a single global model run on the most powerful supercomputer
questions.explain: Metin 'a hybrid future, in which physical models and machine learning work together' diyor. Şık 'work together' yerine 'combine' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Hava tahmininin geleceği büyük ihtimalle nasıl olacak? Dayanak (son cümle): 'Birçok uzman fiziksel modellerle makine öğrenmesinin birlikte çalıştığı karma bir gelecek bekliyor.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: uzmanlar sadece makine öğrenmesi değil, karma yapı bekliyor.
Bilgisayarsız tahmine dönüş metinde yok.
Metinde aşırı olayların göz ardı edileceği yazmıyor; zayıflık olarak anlatılıyor.
Tek bir küresel model metinde önerilmiyor.
questions.tip: Gelecek sorusunda metnin son cümlesine bak; 'expect, likely' kelimeleri cevabı gösterir.

title: The Smallest Atom, the Biggest Threat
text:
High-strength steels have allowed engineers to build lighter bridges, safer cars and deeper offshore wells. Paradoxically, the stronger a steel is, the more vulnerable it tends to be to one of the smallest of all intruders: hydrogen. Because hydrogen atoms are tiny, they can diffuse into the crystal lattice of steel even at room temperature. Sources are surprisingly common, ranging from corrosion reactions and acid pickling to welding with damp electrodes and electroplating.

Once inside, hydrogen atoms tend to accumulate at regions of high stress, such as the tip of a small crack or a notch. There they weaken the bonds between iron atoms and promote cracking at loads that the material would normally carry without difficulty. The resulting failure, known as hydrogen embrittlement, is particularly treacherous because it is often delayed. A bolt may be tightened without any sign of trouble and then fracture hours or even weeks later, after enough hydrogen has migrated to the critical spot.

Although the phenomenon has been studied for more than a century, its exact mechanism is still debated, and several competing theories may each describe part of the truth. In practice, engineers rely on a combination of measures: limiting the hardness of components exposed to hydrogen, baking parts after electroplating so that absorbed hydrogen can escape, and designing microstructures containing fine particles that trap hydrogen harmlessly. The issue is gaining new urgency. If hydrogen is to be transported through existing gas pipelines or stored at high pressure in steel tanks, the compatibility of these materials with hydrogen will have to be demonstrated rather than assumed.

questions.q: It can be understood from the passage that, in terms of hydrogen embrittlement, higher strength in steel ----.
options: completely prevents hydrogen from entering the lattice
makes delayed failures impossible
has no connection with the problem
is achieved mainly by adding hydrogen
generally increases the risk rather than reducing it
questions.explain: Metin 'the stronger a steel is, the more vulnerable it tends to be' diyor. Şık bunu 'generally increases the risk' diye veriyor; 'tends to' şıkta 'generally' olmuş.
questions.anlam: Soru: Hidrojen gevrekliği açısından çeliğin yüksek mukavemeti ne demek? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Çelik ne kadar güçlüyse hidrojene karşı o kadar savunmasız olma eğilimindedir.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: hidrojen oda sıcaklığında bile kafese girebilir.
Metinle çelişiyor: gecikmeli kırılma bu sorunun tipik özelliği.
Metinle çelişiyor: mukavemet ile risk arasında açık bir bağ var.
Metinde mukavemetin hidrojen eklenerek sağlandığı yazmıyor.
questions.tip: 'The more ..., the more ...' kalıbı doğru orantı verir; şıkta 'increases' olarak karşına çıkar.

questions.q: According to the passage, hydrogen embrittlement is especially dangerous because ----.
options: failure may occur long after a component has been loaded
it can be detected only at very high temperatures after the part has been baked
it affects only damp electrodes
it always causes visible deformation before the component finally fractures
it occurs only in steels with low hardness
questions.explain: Metin 'particularly treacherous because it is often delayed' diyor. Şık bunu 'failure may occur long after a component has been loaded' ile anlatıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Hidrojen gevrekliği özellikle neden tehlikeli? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Genellikle gecikmeli olduğu için sinsidir; cıvata saatler ya da haftalar sonra kırılabilir.'
why: Pişirme (baking) hidrojeni çıkarmak için yapılır; tespit için değil.
Nemli elektrot sadece bir hidrojen kaynağı; etkilenen parça değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: kırılma çoğu zaman görünür işaret olmadan olur.
Metinle çelişiyor: risk yüksek mukavemetli, sert çeliklerde fazladır.
questions.tip: 'Especially dangerous because' sorusunda metinde 'particularly ... because' ifadesini ara.

questions.q: The author's main point in the last paragraph is that ----.
options: the mechanism of embrittlement has finally been fully explained by a single accepted theory
gaps in theory remain, yet practical safeguards exist and new uses raise the stakes
existing gas pipelines have already been proven safe for carrying hydrogen at high pressure
baking parts after electroplating increases hydrogen content
hydrogen should never be stored in steel tanks
questions.explain: Paragrafın üç parçası var: teori belirsiz, pratik önlemler var, yeni kullanımlar aciliyet yaratıyor. Şık üçünü birlikte veriyor: 'gaps in theory remain, yet practical safeguards exist and new uses raise the stakes'.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazarın son paragraftaki ana fikri ne? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Mekanizma hâlâ tartışmalı; mühendisler önlemler kullanıyor ve hidrojen boru hatları konuyu daha acil hâle getiriyor.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: mekanizma hâlâ tartışılıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: uyumluluk varsayılmamalı, kanıtlanmalı.
Metinle çelişiyor: pişirme hidrojenin çıkmasını sağlar.
Yazar 'never' demiyor; uyumluluğun gösterilmesi gerektiğini söylüyor.
questions.tip: Paragrafın ana fikri sorulunca paragraftaki her cümle grubunu kapsayan şıkkı seç.

title: Making Steel Without Coal
text:
Steel is indispensable to modern life, but its production is responsible for roughly seven to nine percent of global carbon dioxide emissions. Most of these emissions arise in the blast furnace, where coke made from coal serves both as a fuel and as the agent that removes oxygen from iron ore. Because this chemical role cannot be performed by electricity alone, decarbonising steel is widely regarded as one of the hardest challenges of the energy transition.

One promising route replaces carbon with hydrogen. In direct reduction, iron ore pellets react with a hot reducing gas in a shaft furnace below the melting point of iron, producing a porous solid known as direct reduced iron, or sponge iron. Plants of this type already operate in regions with cheap natural gas, which supplies a mixture of hydrogen and carbon monoxide. If the gas is pure hydrogen produced with renewable electricity, the main by-product becomes water vapour instead of carbon dioxide. The sponge iron is then usually melted in an electric arc furnace.

The obstacles are considerable. Producing enough green hydrogen for a single large steelworks would require vast amounts of renewable electricity. Direct reduction also works best with high-grade ore containing few impurities, and such ore is in limited supply. Furthermore, existing blast furnaces represent enormous investments that companies are reluctant to abandon before the end of their working lives. For these reasons, many producers are pursuing transitional strategies, for instance injecting hydrogen into existing furnaces or capturing carbon dioxide, while pilot plants test whether fully hydrogen-based steelmaking can operate reliably on an industrial scale.

questions.q: According to the passage, decarbonising steel is particularly difficult because ----.
options: steel production accounts for most of the world's carbon dioxide emissions from industry
electric arc furnaces cannot melt iron unless coke is added as an additional fuel
hydrogen reacts too slowly with ore
coal is needed chemically to strip oxygen from the ore, not merely as fuel
iron ore contains no oxygen
questions.explain: Metin kokun 'both as a fuel and as the agent that removes oxygen' olduğunu ve bunun elektrikle yapılamayacağını söylüyor. Şık 'removes oxygen' yerine 'strip oxygen' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Çeliği karbonsuzlaştırmak neden özellikle zor? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Kok hem yakıt hem de cevherden oksijeni alan madde; bu kimyasal görev sadece elektrikle yapılamaz.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: çelik küresel emisyonun yüzde 7-9'u; 'most' yanlış.
Ark ocağı sünger demiri eritir; kok gerektiği yazmıyor.
Hidrojenin yavaş tepkimeye girdiği metinde yok.
Metinle çelişiyor: cevherden oksijen uzaklaştırılıyor, yani oksijen içeriyor.
questions.tip: 'Because' sorusunda 'Because this ... cannot' cümlesini bul; zorluğun sebebi orada.

questions.q: It is stated in the passage that direct reduced iron ----.
options: is made in a blast furnace in which coke removes oxygen from the iron ore
can be produced only with pure hydrogen made from renewable electricity
contains more impurities than any other product
is the final product sold to customers
is produced in solid form without melting the iron
questions.explain: Metin 'below the melting point of iron, producing a porous solid' diyor. Şık bunu 'produced in solid form without melting the iron' ile söylüyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Doğrudan indirgenmiş demir hakkında metinde ne söyleniyor? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Cevher peletleri demirin erime noktasının altında tepkimeye girer ve gözenekli bir katı oluşur.'
why: Yüksek fırın ve kok eski yöntem; doğrudan indirgeme şaft fırınında olur.
Metinle çelişiyor: doğal gazla çalışan tesisler zaten var; 'only' yanlış.
Metinde en fazla safsızlık içerdiği yazmıyor; tersine yüksek kaliteli cevher ister.
Metinle çelişiyor: sünger demir sonra ark ocağında eritilir; son ürün değil.
questions.tip: 'It is stated' sorusunda şıkkı metinde birebir ara; 'only, most' gibi kelimeleri metinle karşılaştır.

questions.q: Which of the following can be inferred about steel producers from the last paragraph?
options: Most of them have already closed their blast furnaces and switched to direct reduction.
They have unlimited access to high-grade ore.
Many favour gradual steps over replacing blast furnaces at once.
They regard fully hydrogen-based steelmaking as proven on an industrial scale.
They are not interested in reducing emissions.
questions.explain: Üreticiler yüksek fırınları erken bırakmak istemiyor ve 'transitional strategies' izliyor. Şık bunu 'favour gradual steps over replacing blast furnaces at once' diye veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Son paragraftan çelik üreticileri hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Birçok üretici geçiş stratejileri izliyor; örneğin mevcut fırınlara hidrojen veriyor ya da CO2 yakalıyor.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: şirketler yüksek fırınları bırakmak istemiyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: yüksek kaliteli cevher sınırlı.
Metinle çelişiyor: pilot tesisler hâlâ bunu test ediyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: geçiş stratejileri emisyonu azaltmak için.
questions.tip: Çıkarım sorusunda 'For these reasons' sonrası cümle genelde cevabı verir.

title: A Star in a Bottle
text:
The Sun shines because, in its core, hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium and release enormous amounts of energy. Reproducing this process on Earth has been a goal of physicists since the 1950s. Fusion fuel is abundant, the reactions produce no carbon dioxide, and, unlike fission reactors, a fusion plant would not generate long-lived radioactive waste in large quantities or be at risk of a runaway chain reaction.

The difficulty lies in the conditions required. Atomic nuclei are positively charged and repel each other, so they must collide at extremely high speeds, which means heating the fuel to temperatures of the order of a hundred million degrees. At such temperatures, matter becomes a plasma that would destroy any container it touched. The most developed approach, the tokamak, holds the plasma in a doughnut-shaped chamber using powerful magnetic fields. An alternative, inertial confinement, fires intense lasers at a tiny fuel pellet to compress and heat it in a fraction of a second.

In December 2022, the National Ignition Facility in the United States reported that a laser experiment had released more fusion energy than the laser light delivered to the target. The achievement was widely celebrated as a historic milestone. Yet it must be interpreted with care: the lasers themselves consumed far more electricity than the fusion reaction produced, and a power plant would need to repeat such reactions many times per second. Meanwhile, the international ITER tokamak under construction in France has faced repeated delays and rising costs. Fusion, critics joke, has always been thirty years away; its supporters reply that the joke is finally becoming outdated.

questions.q: According to the passage, extremely high temperatures are needed for fusion because ----.
options: plasma cools down too quickly when it is held inside powerful magnetic fields
fusion would otherwise produce large amounts of long-lived radioactive waste
lasers cannot operate at low temperatures
like charges make nuclei repel, so they must meet at high speed
hydrogen turns into helium only in the Sun
questions.explain: Metin çekirdeklerin 'positively charged and repel each other, so they must collide at extremely high speeds' olduğunu söylüyor. Şık 'positively charged' yerine 'like charges' (aynı yükler) diyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Füzyon için neden çok yüksek sıcaklık gerekir? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Çekirdekler pozitif yüklüdür ve birbirini iter, bu yüzden çok yüksek hızla çarpışmaları gerekir.'
why: Plazmanın manyetik alanda hızla soğuduğu metinde yok.
Metinle çelişiyor: füzyon uzun ömürlü atığı çok az üretir; sıcaklıkla ilgisi yok.
Lazerlerin çalışma sıcaklığı metinde geçmiyor.
Metin bu süreci Dünya'da yapmaya çalışıyor; 'only in the Sun' yanlış.
questions.tip: Sebep sorusunda 'so' bağlacına bak: 'A, so B' ise B'nin sebebi A'dır.

questions.q: The author warns that the 2022 result should be "interpreted with care" because ----.
options: the experiment was never repeated
the lasers drew far more electricity than the reaction released
the laser light delivered almost no energy to the fuel target during the experiment
ITER in France had already achieved the same result several years earlier
the reaction produced carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Metin 'the lasers themselves consumed far more electricity than the fusion reaction produced' diyor. Şık 'consumed' yerine 'drew', 'produced' yerine 'released' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazar 2022 sonucunun neden 'dikkatle yorumlanması' gerektiğini söylüyor? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Lazerlerin kendisi füzyonun ürettiğinden çok daha fazla elektrik tüketti.'
why: Deneyin tekrarlanmadığı yazmıyor; santralin bunu saniyede çok kez yapması gerektiği yazıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: hedefe verilen lazer ışığından daha fazla enerji çıktı.
Metinle çelişiyor: ITER hâlâ inşa ediliyor ve gecikiyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: füzyon CO2 üretmez.
questions.tip: 'Interpreted with care' gibi uyarıdan sonra gelen iki nokta (:) cevabı açıklar; hemen sonrasını oku.

questions.q: The tone of the final sentence can best be described as ----.
options: cautiously hopeful, while acknowledging past scepticism
deeply pessimistic, suggesting that fusion research will never produce useful power
angry at critics of fusion
completely indifferent to fusion's future
certain, stating that fusion power plants already supply electricity to homes
questions.explain: Cümle önce eski şüpheciliği (şaka) anıyor, sonra destekçilerin umudunu veriyor. Şık bunu 'cautiously hopeful, while acknowledging past scepticism' diye tanımlıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Son cümlenin tonu nasıl? Dayanak (son cümle): 'Eleştirmenler füzyonun hep 30 yıl uzakta olduğunu söyler; destekçiler bu şakanın artık eskidiğini söylüyor.'
why: Cümle sonunda umutlu bir cevap var; 'never' kötümserliği yok.
Eleştirmenlere öfke yok; sadece bir şaka aktarılıyor.
Yazar ilgisiz değil; paragraf boyunca gelişmeleri tartışıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: henüz evlere elektrik veren füzyon santrali yok.
questions.tip: Ton sorusunda cümlede iki taraf varsa (eleştirmen ve destekçi) her ikisini anan şıkkı seç.

title: Fragile Qubits
text:
Ordinary computers process information in bits, each of which is either a zero or a one. Quantum computers use qubits, which can exist in a superposition of both states at once. When several qubits become entangled, their states are linked in such a way that describing one of them independently of the others is no longer possible. In principle, these properties allow a quantum computer to explore certain problems in ways that no classical machine could match, such as simulating complex molecules or factoring very large numbers.

The same features that make qubits powerful also make them extraordinarily fragile. Any unwanted interaction with the environment, whether a stray vibration, a fluctuation in temperature or a passing electromagnetic signal, can disturb the delicate quantum state. This process, known as decoherence, causes the qubit to lose its information, often within a fraction of a second. For this reason, many leading devices operate inside refrigerators cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero and are carefully shielded from outside disturbances.

Even with such precautions, errors are unavoidable. The proposed solution is quantum error correction, in which the information of one reliable "logical" qubit is spread across many physical qubits, so that errors can be detected and fixed without directly measuring, and thereby destroying, the stored information. The cost is steep: estimates suggest that a single logical qubit might require hundreds or even thousands of physical ones. Recent experiments have shown that adding more physical qubits can indeed reduce the error rate, a crucial proof of principle. Nevertheless, the large, fault-tolerant machines needed for the most valuable applications remain, by most estimates, years away.

questions.q: According to the passage, decoherence ----.
options: is the process by which several qubits become entangled with one another
results from undesired contact between qubits and their surroundings
improves the stability of logical qubits by spreading their information widely
takes place only in classical computers
occurs only at room temperature
questions.explain: Metin 'Any unwanted interaction with the environment' durumu bozar ve buna 'decoherence' der. Şık 'unwanted interaction' yerine 'undesired contact', 'environment' yerine 'surroundings' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Metne göre dekoherans nedir? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Çevreyle istenmeyen her etkileşim kuantum durumunu bozabilir; buna dekoherans denir.'
why: Dolanıklık (entanglement) başka bir kavram; dekoherans değil.
Bilgiyi yayma hata düzeltmenin yöntemi; dekoheransın tam tersi bir çözüm.
Metinle çelişiyor: dekoherans kübitlerde, yani kuantum bilgisayarda olur.
Metinle çelişiyor: aşırı soğukta bile olabilir; 'only at room temperature' yanlış.
questions.tip: Tanım sorusunda 'This process, known as X' kalıbını bul; tanım hemen önceki cümlededir.

questions.q: Why does quantum error correction avoid measuring the stored information directly?
options: Because measurement would destroy the information.
Because measurement requires room temperature.
Because physical qubits cannot be measured at all.
Because it would make the computer classical permanently.
Because measurement is too expensive.
questions.explain: Metin 'without directly measuring, and thereby destroying, the stored information' diyor. Yani ölçmek bilgiyi yok eder; şık bunu 'measurement would destroy the information' ile veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Kuantum hata düzeltme saklanan bilgiyi neden doğrudan ölçmez? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Hatalar, bilgiyi doğrudan ölçmeden ve böylece yok etmeden tespit edilir.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: cihazlar mutlak sıfıra yakın soğutuluyor; oda sıcaklığı gerekmiyor.
Fiziksel kübitlerin hiç ölçülemediği yazmıyor.
Bilgisayarın kalıcı olarak klasik olacağı metinde yok.
Pahalılık mantıksal kübit sayısıyla ilgili; ölçümle ilgili değil.
questions.tip: 'thereby' kelimesi 'böylece, bu yüzden' demektir; ondan sonra gelen kelime sonucu verir.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that the recent experiments ----.
options: are promising, though useful large machines are still far off
proved that a single logical qubit needs only one physical qubit to work reliably
showed that adding qubits always increases errors
have already made large fault-tolerant machines widely available to researchers
ended the need for refrigeration
questions.explain: Deney 'a crucial proof of principle' olarak umut veriyor, ama 'Nevertheless ... remain years away' deniyor. Şık ikisini 'promising, though useful large machines are still far off' diye birleştiriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Son paragraftan son deneyler hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Daha fazla fiziksel kübit eklemek hata oranını azalttı... Yine de büyük makineler yıllar uzakta.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: bir mantıksal kübit yüzlerce ya da binlerce fiziksel kübit ister.
Metinle çelişiyor: kübit eklemek hatayı azalttı.
Metinle çelişiyor: büyük makineler hâlâ yıllar uzakta.
Soğutma ihtiyacının bittiği metinde yok.
questions.tip: Paragraf 'olumlu bilgi + Nevertheless' ile bitiyorsa doğru şık 'promising, though ...' gibi iki yönlü olur.

title: Beyond the Genetic Code
text:
Almost every cell in your body contains the same DNA, yet a nerve cell and a liver cell look and behave very differently. The explanation lies not in the genes themselves but in which genes are switched on or off. The study of such heritable changes in gene activity that do not involve alterations to the DNA sequence is called epigenetics.

One of the best-understood mechanisms is DNA methylation, in which small chemical tags called methyl groups are attached to the DNA, usually silencing nearby genes. Another involves the proteins called histones, around which DNA is wound. Chemical modifications to histones can loosen or tighten this packaging, making genes more or less accessible to the machinery that reads them. These patterns are copied when cells divide, which is why a skin cell gives rise to more skin cells rather than to neurons.

What has attracted public interest is evidence that the environment can influence these marks. Diet, stress, smoking and exposure to pollutants have all been associated with changes in methylation. Some studies of people conceived during periods of famine have reported differences in methylation decades later. Claims that such changes are routinely passed on across many human generations, however, deserve caution. In mammals, most epigenetic marks are erased in the germ cells and in the early embryo, and convincing evidence of inheritance over several generations comes mainly from plants and laboratory animals. Epigenetics is therefore best understood not as a rejection of genetics but as an additional layer of regulation that helps explain how a single genome can produce many different outcomes.

questions.q: According to the passage, nerve cells and liver cells differ mainly because ----.
options: they contain completely different DNA sequences inherited from their parents
liver cells have no histones
nerve cells lack methyl groups entirely, while liver cells contain many of them
different sets of genes are active in them
they are produced by different parents
questions.explain: Metin 'which genes are switched on or off' diyor. Şık bunu 'different sets of genes are active in them' ile söylüyor; 'switched on' yerine 'active' kullanılmış.
questions.anlam: Soru: Sinir hücresi ve karaciğer hücresi esas olarak neden farklı? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Açıklama genlerin kendisinde değil, hangi genlerin açık ya da kapalı olduğunda yatıyor.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: hemen her hücrede aynı DNA vardır.
Metinde karaciğer hücrelerinde histon olmadığı yazmıyor.
Metinde sinir hücrelerinde hiç metil grubu olmadığı yazmıyor.
Metin bütün hücrelerin aynı DNA'yı taşıdığını söylüyor; farkı ebeveyne değil gen etkinliğine bağlıyor.
questions.tip: 'not in A but in B' kalıbında cevap her zaman B kısmıdır.

questions.q: The author refers to studies of people conceived during famine in order to ----.
options: prove that epigenetic changes are always inherited for many generations
give an example of possible environmental effects on epigenetic marks
show that diet has no influence on methylation
argue that genetics should be rejected
explain how histones are modified
questions.explain: Paragraf 'the environment can influence these marks' diye başlıyor ve kıtlık çalışmasını örnek veriyor. Şık bunu 'example of possible environmental effects on epigenetic marks' diye söylüyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazar kıtlık döneminde ana rahmine düşen insanlarla ilgili çalışmalardan neden söz ediyor? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Çevrenin bu işaretleri etkileyebileceğine dair kanıt' konusunun örneği olarak veriliyor.
why: Metinle çelişiyor: yazar nesiller boyu aktarım iddialarına temkinli bakıyor; 'always' yanlış.
Metinle çelişiyor: beslenme metilasyonla ilişkilendirildi.
Metinle çelişiyor: epigenetik genetiğin reddi değil, ek bir katman.
Histon değişikliği 2. paragrafta; kıtlık örneğiyle ilgisi yok.
questions.tip: 'Refers to X in order to' sorusunda X'ten önceki genel cümleyi bul; X onun örneğidir.

questions.q: Which of the following best summarises the author's view in the last part of the passage?
options: Epigenetics proves that genes play no real role in how cells develop into different types.
Epigenetic marks are never erased in mammals.
Plants and humans inherit epigenetic marks across many generations in exactly the same way.
Epigenetics adds to genetics, and claims of human inheritance need caution.
Environmental factors have no connection with epigenetic changes.
questions.explain: Yazar iki şey söylüyor: aktarım iddiaları 'deserve caution' ve epigenetik 'an additional layer'. Şık ikisini 'adds to genetics, and claims of human inheritance need caution' ile birleştiriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Metnin son kısmında yazarın görüşünü en iyi hangisi özetler? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'İnsanda nesiller boyu aktarım iddialarına temkinli olmak gerek... Epigenetik genetiği reddetmez, ek bir düzenleme katmanıdır.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: epigenetik genetiği reddetmez.
Metinle çelişiyor: memelilerde çoğu işaret silinir; 'never' yanlış.
Metinle çelişiyor: güçlü kanıt bitki ve laboratuvar hayvanlarından; insanla aynı değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: çevre metilasyon değişiklikleriyle ilişkilendirildi.
questions.tip: Özet sorusunda son kısmın iki ana mesajını bul; ikisini birden içeren şık doğrudur.

title: The Other Carbon Problem
text:
Discussions of carbon dioxide usually focus on its role in warming the planet. Yet roughly a quarter of the carbon dioxide released by human activities does not stay in the atmosphere at all; it dissolves in the oceans. This uptake has slowed climate change considerably, but it comes at a chemical cost. When carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater, it forms carbonic acid, which releases hydrogen ions and lowers the water's pH. Since the beginning of the industrial era, the average pH of surface seawater has fallen by about 0.1 units. Because the pH scale is logarithmic, this apparently small change corresponds to an increase in acidity of roughly thirty percent.

The consequences are most serious for organisms that build shells or skeletons from calcium carbonate, including corals, oysters, sea snails and some plankton. The extra hydrogen ions combine with carbonate ions, reducing the amount available for building shells. Under these conditions, organisms must spend more energy to grow, and in extreme cases existing shells may begin to dissolve. Laboratory experiments have shown deformed shells in larvae of some species, and natural sites near volcanic vents, where carbon dioxide bubbles from the seabed, offer a preview of how communities may change, with fewer calcifying species and more seaweeds.

Not every species is equally affected, and some appear surprisingly tolerant. The effects also interact with warming and with the loss of oxygen in the oceans, which makes predictions difficult. What is clear, however, is that ocean acidification cannot be solved by approaches that cool the planet without reducing carbon dioxide, such as reflecting sunlight back into space. Only lowering emissions addresses both problems at once.

questions.q: The author mentions that the pH scale is logarithmic in order to ----.
options: argue that the fall of about 0.1 units in pH is too small to have any real effect
explain how carbon dioxide dissolved in seawater warms the atmosphere above it
prove that seawater has become alkaline
show that a slight numerical shift means a large rise in acidity
describe how pH is measured in laboratories
questions.explain: Metin 'this apparently small change corresponds to an increase in acidity of roughly thirty percent' diyor. Şık 'apparently small change' yerine 'slight numerical shift', 'increase' yerine 'large rise' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazar pH ölçeğinin logaritmik olduğunu neden söylüyor? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Ölçek logaritmik olduğu için bu küçük görünen değişim asitlikte yaklaşık yüzde 30 artış demek.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: yazar küçük değişimin aslında büyük etki olduğunu söylüyor.
pH ve atmosfer ısınması burada ilişkilendirilmiyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: deniz suyu daha asidik oluyor, alkali değil.
Laboratuvarda pH ölçümü metinde anlatılmıyor.
questions.tip: 'Because' ile verilen bir bilgi, sonra 'this apparently...' diye bağlanıyorsa amaç o cümlenin sonucunu göstermektir.

questions.q: According to the passage, the natural sites near volcanic vents are useful because they ----.
options: prevent the acidification of the surrounding ocean by releasing carbonate into it
give a glimpse of future marine communities under more carbon dioxide
are unusually rich in calcifying species such as corals, oysters and sea snails
contain no seaweeds
release oxygen into the water
questions.explain: Metin 'offer a preview of how communities may change' diyor. Şık 'preview' yerine 'glimpse of future marine communities' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Volkanik bacalar yakınındaki doğal alanlar neden yararlı? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Deniz tabanından CO2 çıkan bu alanlar toplulukların nasıl değişeceğine dair bir ön izleme sunuyor.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: bacalar CO2 salar, asitlenmeyi önlemez.
Metinle çelişiyor: bu alanlarda kireçlenen türler daha az.
Metinle çelişiyor: bu alanlarda daha fazla deniz yosunu var.
Metinde oksijen salındığı yazmıyor; CO2 çıkıyor.
questions.tip: 'Useful because' sorusunda metinde 'offer, provide, show' gibi fiilleri ara.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that reflecting sunlight into space ----.
options: is the only approach that can solve both warming and acidification at the same time
increases carbon dioxide emissions directly and therefore worsens ocean acidification
might reduce warming but would not stop ocean acidification
has already reversed acidification
makes all marine species tolerant
questions.explain: Işığı yansıtmak gezegeni soğutabilir ama CO2'yi azaltmaz, yani asitlenmeyi durdurmaz. Şık bunu 'might reduce warming but would not stop ocean acidification' diye veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Güneş ışığını uzaya yansıtmak hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Okyanus asitlenmesi, CO2'yi azaltmadan gezegeni soğutan yaklaşımlarla çözülemez.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: ikisini birden çözen tek yol emisyonu azaltmak.
Metinde yansıtmanın emisyonu doğrudan artırdığı yazmıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: bu yöntem asitlenmeyi çözemez.
Metinle çelişiyor: türler eşit etkilenmiyor; 'all tolerant' yok.
questions.tip: Çıkarım sorusunda 'such as' ile verilen örneği bul; örnek, önceki genel kurala uyar.

title: The Missing Mass
text:
In the 1970s, the American astronomer Vera Rubin and her colleagues measured how fast stars and gas move around the centres of spiral galaxies. According to Newton's laws, objects far from the bright centre, where most of the visible matter lies, should orbit more slowly, just as Neptune moves more slowly around the Sun than Mercury does. Instead, Rubin found that the orbital speeds remained roughly constant far into the outer regions. If only visible matter were present, these galaxies should have flown apart long ago.

The most widely accepted explanation is that galaxies are embedded in vast halos of dark matter, a form of matter that exerts gravity but neither emits nor absorbs light. Supporting evidence has since come from several independent directions: the way clusters of galaxies bend the light of more distant objects, the pattern of tiny temperature variations in the cosmic microwave background, and computer simulations showing that the large-scale structure of the universe could not have formed in the available time without additional mass. Taken together, these observations suggest that dark matter outweighs ordinary matter by a factor of about five.

What dark matter actually consists of, however, remains unknown. For decades, a leading candidate was a class of heavy particles that interact only weakly with ordinary matter, but increasingly sensitive underground detectors have so far failed to observe them. A minority of physicists argue that the problem lies not in missing matter but in our theory of gravity, which may need modification at very low accelerations. Such theories explain galaxy rotation well but struggle to account for observations of galaxy clusters. The debate illustrates how science often advances: a single unexpected measurement can expose a gap that takes generations to fill.

questions.q: Rubin's observations were surprising because ----.
options: Neptune was found to move faster than Mercury, contrary to the predictions of Newton's laws
spiral galaxies were shown to contain no gas
outer stars orbited faster than visible matter alone could explain
the spiral galaxies she observed were actually flying apart at very high speeds
Newton's laws were confirmed exactly
questions.explain: Newton'a göre dıştaki yıldızlar yavaşlamalıydı ama hızlar sabit kaldı. Yani görünür maddenin açıklayabileceğinden hızlı döndüler; şık bunu söylüyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Rubin'in gözlemleri neden şaşırtıcıydı? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Yörünge hızları dış bölgelere kadar yaklaşık sabit kaldı; sadece görünür madde olsaydı galaksiler dağılırdı.'
why: Neptün ve Merkür sadece bir benzetme; Neptün yavaş hareket eder.
Metinle çelişiyor: Rubin yıldızların ve gazın hızını ölçtü.
Metinle çelişiyor: galaksiler dağılmıyor; sadece görünür madde olsaydı dağılmaları gerekirdi.
Metinle çelişiyor: sonuçlar Newton'un tahminine uymadı.
questions.tip: 'Surprising because' sorusunda 'Instead' kelimesini bul; beklenen ile bulunan arasındaki fark cevaptır.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT presented as evidence for dark matter?
options: The way galaxy clusters bend the light coming from more distant objects
Temperature variations in the cosmic microwave background
Simulations of the formation of large-scale structure
Underground detection of heavy, weakly interacting particles
The roughly constant speeds of stars in the outer regions of spiral galaxies
questions.explain: Ağır parçacıklar yeraltında hiç tespit edilmedi; yani bu bir kanıt değil, eksik kalan bir arayış. Diğer dört şık metinde kanıt olarak geçiyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Hangisi karanlık maddenin kanıtı olarak SUNULMUYOR? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Giderek hassaslaşan yeraltı dedektörleri bu parçacıkları şimdiye kadar gözlemleyemedi.'
why: Bu kanıt 2. paragrafta açıkça sayılıyor; yani sunuluyor.
Bu kanıt 2. paragrafta açıkça sayılıyor; yani sunuluyor.
Bu kanıt 2. paragrafta açıkça sayılıyor; yani sunuluyor.
Bu Rubin'in ilk bulgusu ve karanlık madde fikrini başlatan kanıt.
questions.tip: 'NOT' sorusunda her şıkkı metinde işaretle; bulamadığın ya da tersi söylenen şıkkı seç.

questions.q: The author's purpose in the last sentence is to ----.
options: draw a general lesson about how scientific progress works
reject the existence of dark matter
prove that our theory of gravity must be modified at very low accelerations
criticise Rubin's measurements
suggest that the debate about the nature of dark matter has now been settled
questions.explain: Yazar 'The debate illustrates how science often advances' deyip genel bir ders çıkarıyor. Şık bunu 'draw a general lesson about how scientific progress works' diye söylüyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazarın son cümledeki amacı ne? Dayanak (son cümle): 'Bu tartışma bilimin nasıl ilerlediğini gösteriyor: tek bir beklenmedik ölçüm, doldurulması nesiller süren bir boşluğu açığa çıkarabilir.'
why: Yazar karanlık maddeyi reddetmiyor; en çok kabul gören açıklama diyor.
Kütleçekimi değişikliği azınlık görüşü; yazar bunu kanıtlamıyor.

title: The Drifting Continents
text:
In 1912, the German meteorologist Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once been joined in a single landmass and had slowly drifted apart. His evidence was varied and, in hindsight, persuasive. The coastlines of South America and Africa fit together like pieces of a puzzle; identical fossils of land-dwelling reptiles appeared on continents now separated by oceans; and rock formations and traces of ancient glaciers lined up when the continents were reassembled.

Most geologists nevertheless rejected the idea for several decades. Their main objection was not to Wegener's observations but to his mechanism. He suggested that continents ploughed through the ocean floor, pushed by forces related to Earth's rotation, yet physicists calculated that such forces were far too weak. Without a plausible cause, many scientists found it easier to imagine vanished land bridges that had once connected the continents. It did not help that Wegener was an outsider to geology.

The breakthrough came from the ocean floor itself. In the 1950s and 1960s, surveys revealed a vast system of underwater mountain ridges and, alongside them, symmetrical stripes of rock with alternating magnetic orientations. These stripes were explained by the idea that new crust forms at the ridges and spreads outward, recording reversals of Earth's magnetic field as it cools. Combined with the discovery that old crust sinks back into the mantle at deep ocean trenches, this led to the theory of plate tectonics. Continents, it turned out, do not plough through the seafloor; they ride on moving plates. Wegener, who died on an expedition to Greenland in 1930, did not live to see his central idea vindicated.

questions.q: According to the passage, most geologists rejected Wegener's idea mainly because ----.
options: he failed to provide a believable cause for the drifting of continents
his fossil evidence was later shown to be false by physicists who studied the reptiles
the coastlines of the continents did not match
he had already discovered the magnetic stripes on the ocean floor but misinterpreted them
he was a famous geologist with rival theories
questions.explain: Metin 'not to Wegener's observations but to his mechanism' ve 'Without a plausible cause' diyor. Şık 'plausible' yerine 'believable cause' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Jeologlar Wegener'in fikrini esas olarak neden reddetti? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Ana itirazları gözlemlerine değil, öne sürdüğü mekanizmaya idi... Makul bir sebep olmadan...'

Manyetik şeritler 1950-60'larda, Wegener öldükten sonra bulundu.

questions.tip: 'not to A but to B' kalıbında cevap B'dir; 'main objection' cümlesini bul.

questions.q: The magnetic stripes on the ocean floor are important because they ----.

title: Chemicals That Refuse to Break Down
text:
Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly known as PFAS, are a family of several thousand synthetic chemicals that have been produced since the 1940s. Their defining feature is the bond between carbon and fluorine, one of the strongest in organic chemistry. This bond gives PFAS remarkable properties: they repel both water and oil, withstand high temperatures and resist chemical attack. As a result, they have been used in non-stick cookware, waterproof clothing, food packaging and fire-fighting foams.

The very stability that makes PFAS so useful also makes them a problem. Because natural processes break them down extremely slowly, if at all, they have earned the nickname "forever chemicals". They have now been detected in rainwater, soil, wildlife and the blood of most people tested in industrialised countries. Some well-studied PFAS have been linked to effects on the immune system, raised cholesterol and certain cancers, which has prompted regulators to restrict them and to set increasingly strict limits for drinking water.

Removing PFAS once they are in the environment is difficult and expensive. Activated carbon filters and specialised resins can capture many of them from water, but this only transfers the chemicals to another material that must then be disposed of. Destroying them generally requires very high temperatures or energy-intensive treatments, and researchers are investigating methods that break the carbon-fluorine bond under milder conditions. Many scientists argue that, given the size of the chemical family, regulating substances one at a time is too slow. They propose treating PFAS as a single class and limiting their use to applications that are essential and for which no safer alternatives exist.

questions.q: According to the passage, the carbon-fluorine bond is responsible for ----.
options: both the usefulness of PFAS and the fact that they persist
the low cost of fire-fighting foams
the rapid breakdown of PFAS in rainwater, soil and the bodies of wildlife
the ability of PFAS to absorb both water and oil at high temperatures
the use of PFAS as a medicine

title: The Bridge That Danced
text:
When the Tacoma Narrows Bridge opened in the state of Washington in July 1940, it was the third-longest suspension bridge in the world and a showcase of elegant, economical design. Its deck was remarkably slender: instead of a deep, open steel truss, it was stiffened by shallow solid plate girders, which made it light and graceful but also unusually flexible. Even during construction, workers noticed that the deck moved up and down in moderate winds, and the bridge soon acquired the nickname "Galloping Gertie". Drivers sometimes crossed it for the thrill of watching cars ahead disappear and reappear in the waves of the roadway.

On 7 November 1940, only four months after opening, a steady wind of roughly 65 kilometres per hour set the deck into a violent twisting motion. For about an hour, the roadway rotated back and forth until cables and supports failed and the central span collapsed into the water below. Nobody was killed, although a dog trapped in an abandoned car was lost.

The collapse is often presented in textbooks as a simple case of resonance, in which the wind pushed the bridge at its natural frequency. Engineers now regard this explanation as incomplete. A steady wind does not supply a regular periodic push in the way that a child is pushed on a swing. Instead, the twisting motion of the deck altered the airflow around it, and the airflow in turn fed energy back into the motion, a self-excited phenomenon known as aeroelastic flutter. The failure transformed bridge engineering: designers began testing models in wind tunnels and favouring deeper or aerodynamically shaped decks, practices that remain standard today.

title: Strength Through Deformation
text:
When a steel strip is passed between the rolls of a cold mill at room temperature, its thickness is reduced and its length increased, yet the most consequential change takes place at a scale invisible to the naked eye. Plastic deformation in metals proceeds through the movement of dislocations, which are line defects in the crystal lattice. As the reduction increases, new dislocations are generated in enormous numbers, whereby they become entangled with one another and obstruct each other's motion. The result, known as work hardening or strain hardening, is a marked rise in yield strength and hardness, which is accompanied by a corresponding loss of ductility.

For the producer, this phenomenon is a mixed blessing. On the one hand, it enables high-strength thin gauges to be manufactured without costly alloying additions; on the other hand, a heavily reduced strip becomes so hard and brittle that further reduction would demand excessive rolling forces and could lead to edge cracking. It is for this reason that cold-rolled coils are commonly subjected to annealing, a heat treatment during which new, strain-free grains nucleate and grow, thereby restoring the formability required for operations such as deep drawing.

Notwithstanding its apparent simplicity, the balance between hardening and annealing is a matter of considerable precision. The final properties depend not only on the total reduction but also on the annealing temperature and time, whereas a light final pass, referred to as temper rolling or skin passing, is frequently applied in order to eliminate the yield-point elongation that would otherwise produce unsightly surface markings known as Lüders bands during forming.

title: A Zinc Shield
text:
Hot-dip galvanizing is one of the oldest and most widely used methods of protecting steel from corrosion. In this process, a cleaned steel part or a continuous strip is immersed in a bath of molten zinc at a temperature of about 450 °C. During immersion, the zinc reacts with the iron at the surface and forms a series of zinc–iron alloy layers, which are covered by an outer layer of almost pure zinc. Because these layers are metallurgically bonded to the steel, the coating does not peel off easily, unlike many paints.

Zinc protects steel in two ways. First, it acts as a physical barrier that keeps water and oxygen away from the surface. Second, and more importantly, zinc is more reactive than iron. If the coating is scratched and the steel underneath is exposed, the zinc around the damaged area corrodes in preference to the steel. In other words, zinc sacrifices itself, which is why this mechanism is called sacrificial or cathodic protection. As a result, small scratches do not lead to the spread of rust under the coating.

In continuous galvanizing lines for automotive sheet, small amounts of aluminium are added to the bath. The aluminium forms a thin layer between the steel and the zinc and limits the growth of brittle zinc–iron compounds, so the coated sheet can be bent and pressed without cracking. The protection does not last forever, however: its lifetime depends mainly on the coating thickness and the aggressiveness of the environment.

title: The Zone Next to the Weld
text:
In fusion welding, the attention of the inspector is naturally drawn to the weld bead itself, yet many failures originate not in the solidified weld metal but in the narrow band of base metal adjacent to it. This region, termed the heat-affected zone (HAZ), never melts; nevertheless, it is heated to temperatures high enough to transform its microstructure and is then cooled at a rate that is dictated largely by the plate thickness, the preheat and the heat input of the process.

The consequences of this thermal cycle vary considerably across the zone. Close to the fusion line, where peak temperatures approach the melting point, austenite grains grow coarse, and rapid cooling may produce martensite, a hard but brittle phase. Further away, the steel may merely be tempered or partially transformed. In carbon and low-alloy steels, a hard HAZ combined with hydrogen introduced from moisture in consumables and with residual tensile stresses constitutes the classic recipe for cold cracking, which may appear hours after welding has been completed.

To predict this susceptibility, engineers frequently use a carbon equivalent, a formula in which the effects of manganese, chromium, molybdenum and other elements on hardenability are expressed relative to that of carbon. The higher the carbon equivalent, the greater the need for preheating, which slows the cooling rate and allows hydrogen to diffuse out. In modern thermomechanically processed steels, by contrast, strength is achieved through grain refinement rather than high carbon content, thereby allowing such steels to be welded with little or no preheat, although excessive heat input can still soften their HAZ.

options: The Invention of Fusion Welding

title: Materials One Atom Thick
text:
In 2004, two researchers at the University of Manchester used ordinary adhesive tape to peel thin flakes from a piece of graphite, the material found in pencils. By repeating the process, they eventually obtained graphene, a sheet of carbon atoms only one atom thick, arranged in a honeycomb pattern. The discovery earned them the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2010 and started a wave of research into so-called two-dimensional materials.

Graphene has a remarkable combination of properties. It is one of the strongest materials ever measured, yet it is flexible and almost transparent. It conducts heat and electricity extremely well, because electrons can travel through it with very little scattering. These properties are not simply those of graphite on a smaller scale; they arise precisely because the material is so thin that its electrons are confined to a single plane.

Despite the excitement, turning graphene into commercial products has proved slower than many expected. The tape method produces only tiny flakes, while large sheets grown on metal foils often contain defects and must be transferred carefully to other surfaces. Moreover, graphene has no band gap, which makes it difficult to use directly in digital transistors that need to be switched fully off. Today, most commercial uses involve adding small amounts of graphene to other materials, for example to improve the strength of polymers or the conductivity of coatings and battery electrodes.

questions.q: The passage mainly discusses ----.
options: the advantages of digital transistors over graphene

methods of producing large defect-free metal foils

title: Fibres in a Matrix
text:
A composite material combines two or more different materials in order to obtain properties that none of them has on its own. In carbon-fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP), thin carbon fibres, each several times thinner than a human hair, are embedded in a matrix of plastic resin, usually epoxy. The fibres carry most of the load, while the matrix holds them in position, transfers stress between them and protects them from damage.

The main attraction of CFRP is its high strength and stiffness relative to its weight. For this reason, it has become a key material in aircraft, racing cars and wind-turbine blades. In some modern airliners, composites account for about half of the structural weight, which reduces fuel consumption considerably.

However, composites behave quite differently from metals. Because the fibres are aligned in particular directions, the material is very strong along the fibres but much weaker across them. Designers therefore stack layers with fibres in different orientations to suit the expected loads. In addition, damage in composites can be hard to detect. An impact, such as a dropped tool, may leave almost no mark on the surface while causing the internal layers to separate, a defect known as delamination. Inspection methods such as ultrasonic testing are needed to find such hidden damage. Finally, recycling remains a problem, since the cured resin cannot simply be melted and reshaped like many other plastics.

questions.q: According to the passage, the matrix in CFRP ----.
options: can easily be melted and reshaped after curing
is several times thinner than a human hair
carries most of the load applied to the material
keeps the fibres in place and transfers stress between them
makes the material equally strong both along and across the fibres
questions.explain: Metin 'the matrix holds them in position, transfers stress between them' diyor. Şık 'holds in position' yerine 'keeps the fibres in place' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: CFRP'de matris ne yapar? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Matris lifleri yerinde tutar, aralarında gerilmeyi aktarır ve onları korur.'

Yükün çoğunu lifler taşır; matris değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: malzeme lif yönünde güçlü, enine zayıf.
questions.tip: İki bileşen anlatılırken 'while' ile ayrılan cümlede her görevin hangi bileşene ait olduğunu işaretle.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that a CFRP part with all its fibres aligned in one direction ----.
options: would not need ultrasonic inspection

title: Metals That Endure the Fire
text:
The efficiency of a gas turbine rises with the temperature of the gas entering it, which explains why the first-stage turbine blades of a modern jet engine operate in a gas stream considerably hotter than the melting point of the alloy from which they are made. That they survive at all is attributable to nickel-based superalloys, combined with elaborate internal cooling channels and ceramic thermal barrier coatings.

The strength of these alloys at high temperature derives principally from a fine dispersion of a precipitate known as gamma prime, an ordered compound of nickel with aluminium and titanium. Because dislocations can pass through these ordered particles only with great difficulty, the alloy resists creep, the slow, time-dependent deformation that would otherwise cause a blade rotating at high speed to stretch until it rubbed against the engine casing. Remarkably, the strength of gamma prime actually increases with temperature over a certain range, a property that is unusual among metallic materials.

Advances in processing have been as decisive as those in composition. Grain boundaries, being weak at high temperatures, act as preferred sites for creep damage; consequently, manufacturers progressed from conventionally cast blades to directionally solidified ones, in which grains are aligned with the principal stress, and ultimately to single-crystal blades, from which grain boundaries are eliminated altogether. Elements such as rhenium further improved creep resistance, although their scarcity and price have prompted research into alloys that achieve comparable performance with smaller additions, whereas ceramic matrix composites are being introduced in some engine parts as a potential successor.

questions.q: According to the passage, turbine blades can operate in gas hotter than their melting point ----.
options: because gamma prime melts at a lower temperature than nickel
owing to a combination of superalloys, internal cooling and ceramic coatings
only when they are made of ceramic matrix composites
since the efficiency of the turbine decreases at high temperature
because the addition of rhenium raises the melting point of the alloy above the gas temperature

title: Solar Cells from a Mineral's Structure
text:
For several decades, crystalline silicon has dominated the photovoltaic market, its efficiency having crept upwards to the point at which commercial modules convert well over twenty percent of incident sunlight into electricity. Since around 2009, however, a class of materials named after the mineral perovskite has attracted extraordinary attention, the efficiency of laboratory cells made from them having risen from under four percent to levels rivalling silicon in little more than a decade, a pace of improvement without precedent in the field.

The appeal of these materials lies not only in their performance but also in the manner in which they can be produced. Whereas silicon wafers require purification and crystal growth at very high temperatures, perovskite layers can be deposited from solution at modest temperatures, potentially by printing techniques, which could substantially lower manufacturing costs. Moreover, because the band gap of a perovskite can be tuned by adjusting its composition, a perovskite layer can be stacked on top of a silicon cell to form a tandem device that captures a broader part of the solar spectrum than either material could on its own.

Notwithstanding these advantages, the technology faces formidable obstacles before it can be deployed widely. The most efficient compositions degrade when exposed to moisture, heat and even prolonged illumination, so that their lifetime falls far short of the twenty-five years customarily guaranteed for silicon modules. Many also contain lead, raising concerns about toxicity should modules be damaged or disposed of improperly. Consequently, much current research is directed less at increasing efficiency further than at achieving stability and safe encapsulation.

title: Batteries Made of Water and Hills
text:
As the share of wind and solar power grows, electricity grids need ways to store energy when production is high and release it when demand rises. The oldest and still by far the largest form of grid-scale storage is pumped-storage hydropower. It accounts for the great majority of the world's installed storage capacity, even though batteries are now growing rapidly.

The principle is simple. A pumped-storage plant has two reservoirs at different heights. When electricity is cheap and plentiful, for example on a sunny afternoon or a windy night, the plant uses it to pump water from the lower reservoir to the upper one. When demand is high, the water is allowed to flow back down through turbines, which generate electricity again. Typically, about 70 to 80 percent of the energy used for pumping is recovered, so the plant does not create energy but shifts it in time.

Pumped storage has important advantages. Plants can operate for decades, they can store energy for many hours, and they can respond to changes in demand within minutes. However, they require suitable geography, with a large height difference between two sites, and building them involves high initial costs and long construction times. Large reservoirs can also affect local ecosystems. To overcome some of these problems, engineers are studying closed-loop systems that are not connected to rivers, as well as designs that use old mines or the sea as the lower reservoir.

questions.q: According to the passage, a pumped-storage plant generates electricity when ----.
options: water is pumped from the lower reservoir to the upper one
water flows from the upper reservoir down through turbines
electricity is cheap and plentiful
the two reservoirs are at the same height

questions.explain: Metin 'the water is allowed to flow back down through turbines, which generate electricity' diyor. Şık bunu 'water flows from the upper reservoir down through turbines' ile veriyor.

title: Heat from Dry Rock
text:
Geothermal energy has conventionally been confined to regions in which three conditions coincide: high subsurface temperatures, naturally permeable rock and abundant underground fluid. Such hydrothermal settings, typified by Iceland, parts of Indonesia and western Türkiye, are geographically limited, which explains why geothermal power, despite offering continuous output independent of weather, supplies only a small fraction of global electricity.

Enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) are intended to remove two of these conditions from the equation. Because temperature increases with depth almost everywhere, sufficiently hot rock can in principle be reached by drilling deep enough; what is generally lacking is a network of fractures through which water could circulate. In an EGS, water is injected at high pressure in order to open or extend fractures in the hot rock, thereby creating an artificial reservoir. Cold water pumped down one well is heated as it passes through the fractures and is returned to the surface through another, where its heat is used to generate electricity before it is reinjected.

The concept is decades old, but its progress has been hampered by high drilling costs and by induced seismicity. In 2006, an EGS project beneath the Swiss city of Basel was suspended after the injection triggered a series of small earthquakes that alarmed residents, and an earthquake in Pohang, South Korea, in 2017 was subsequently linked to a nearby geothermal project. Recently, however, the adaptation of horizontal drilling and multistage stimulation techniques from the oil and gas industry has revived interest, suggesting that the technology might eventually make geothermal power available far beyond volcanic regions.

title: Turbines in Each Other's Shadow
text:
Offshore wind farms have become one of the fastest-growing sources of renewable electricity, especially in northern Europe. Winds at sea are generally stronger and steadier than on land, and very large turbines, some with blades longer than a football field, can be transported by ship more easily than by road.

When a turbine extracts energy from the wind, however, the air behind it moves more slowly and becomes more turbulent. This region of disturbed air is called the wake. A turbine standing in the wake of another produces less power than it would in undisturbed wind, and the extra turbulence increases the fatigue loads on its blades. In large wind farms, these losses can reduce total energy production by around ten percent or more, depending on the layout and the wind direction.

Researchers have found that wakes at sea can stretch for tens of kilometres, partly because the smooth sea surface mixes the air less than rough land does. As more farms are built close together, the wake of one farm may reduce the output of its neighbour, which raises new legal and economic questions. To reduce wake losses, engineers increase the spacing between turbines and arrange them carefully relative to the main wind direction. A newer approach, called wake steering, deliberately turns the front turbines slightly away from the wind, so that their wakes are pushed aside. Although the front turbines then produce a little less, the farm as a whole can produce more.

title: Light in Step
text:
The word 'laser' is an acronym for 'light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation'. The idea behind it goes back to 1917, when Albert Einstein showed theoretically that an atom in an excited state can be triggered by an incoming photon to emit a second photon identical to the first. The new photon has the same wavelength, direction and phase, so the two waves travel in step. This process is called stimulated emission.

Normally, most atoms in a material are in their lowest energy state, so incoming light is absorbed rather than amplified. To make a laser work, energy must be pumped into the material, by an electric current, a flash lamp or another laser, until more atoms are in the excited state than in the lower state. This unusual condition is known as population inversion. The material is placed between two mirrors, one of which lets a small fraction of the light escape. Light bouncing back and forth between the mirrors is amplified again and again, and the escaping beam is the laser output.

The first working laser was built by Theodore Maiman in 1960 using a ruby crystal. At the time, it was described as 'a solution looking for a problem'. Today, lasers are used in barcode scanners, fibre-optic communication, eye surgery and the cutting and welding of metals. Their usefulness comes from the fact that the light is highly concentrated and can be focused onto a very small spot.

title: Listening to Spacetime
text:
Among the predictions of Einstein's general theory of relativity, published in 1915, was the existence of gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of spacetime produced by accelerating masses. Einstein himself doubted that they would ever be detected, and with good reason: even the waves emitted by the most violent cosmic events alter distances on Earth by an amount far smaller than the diameter of a proton.

Indirect evidence was obtained from the late 1970s onwards, when observations of a pair of neutron stars orbiting each other showed that their orbit was shrinking at precisely the rate expected if the system were losing energy through gravitational radiation. Direct detection, however, required instruments of almost unimaginable sensitivity. The Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) consists of two L-shaped detectors, each with arms four kilometres long, along which laser beams travel back and forth between mirrors. A passing wave stretches one arm while compressing the other, thereby altering the pattern formed when the beams are recombined. Since local disturbances such as traffic or seismic activity can mimic such a signal, the two detectors were built some 3,000 kilometres apart, so that a genuine wave would register at both within milliseconds.

On 14 September 2015, both detectors recorded a signal that matched the waveform predicted for the merger of two black holes about 1.3 billion light-years away. The detection, which earned three of the project's leaders the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics, did more than confirm a century-old prediction: it opened an entirely new means of observing the universe, one that does not depend on light and can therefore reveal events that emit little or none.
