title: Electricity from Pressure
text:
In 1880, the brothers Pierre and Jacques Curie discovered that certain crystals, such as quartz, produce an electric voltage when they are squeezed or bent. This phenomenon is called the piezoelectric effect, from the Greek word 'piezein', meaning to press. Soon afterwards, it was predicted and then confirmed that the effect also works in reverse: when a voltage is applied to such a crystal, it changes shape slightly.

The effect occurs only in materials whose crystal structure lacks a centre of symmetry. When the crystal is deformed, the positive and negative charges inside it are displaced relative to each other, and a voltage appears across the material. In symmetrical crystals, these displacements cancel out, so no voltage is produced.

Both forms of the effect are widely used today. In a quartz watch, an alternating voltage makes a tiny quartz crystal vibrate at a very stable frequency, which the electronics use to keep time. Gas lighters produce a spark when a spring-loaded hammer strikes a piezoelectric crystal. Ultrasound imaging in medicine and sonar at sea rely on piezoelectric elements that convert electrical signals into sound waves and back again. In industry, piezoelectric sensors measure pressure, vibration and force, for example in engines or rolling mills. Researchers are also exploring ways to harvest energy from footsteps or vibrations, although the amount of power produced in this way is usually small.

title: The Missing Colour
text:
A light-emitting diode generates light when electrons, driven across the junction between two differently doped regions of a semiconductor, recombine with holes and release their excess energy as photons. The colour of the emitted light is determined by the band gap of the semiconductor, that is, by the energy separating the states in which electrons are bound from those in which they are free to conduct: the wider the gap, the more energetic the photons and the shorter their wavelength.

Red and green LEDs were available by the 1960s and 1970s, but an efficient blue one, which was indispensable for producing white light, proved elusive for some three decades. The obvious candidate, gallium nitride, possessed a suitably wide band gap, yet it was notoriously difficult to grow as high-quality crystals, and producing the positively doped (p-type) form of the material, without which no diode could function, defeated most researchers. Many laboratories accordingly abandoned the material in favour of alternatives that later turned out to be dead ends.

The breakthrough came in the late 1980s and early 1990s from Isamu Akasaki and Hiroshi Amano, who grew high-quality gallium nitride on a thin buffer layer and achieved p-type doping, and from Shuji Nakamura, who developed a more practical industrial process. Combining a blue LED with a phosphor that converts part of its light into yellow yields white light, which made LED lamps possible. Since such lamps consume a fraction of the electricity required by incandescent bulbs, the three researchers were awarded the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics, the committee having emphasised the invention's contribution to energy saving rather than its scientific novelty alone.

options: the band gap of the semiconductor from which it is made

title: Mirror-Image Molecules
text:
Many organic molecules exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other yet cannot be superimposed, much as a left hand cannot be placed exactly over a right one. Such molecules are termed chiral, and the two forms, called enantiomers, share virtually all physical properties, including melting point and solubility, differing only in the direction in which they rotate polarised light and in the way they interact with other chiral substances.

This last distinction is of profound consequence for biology, since the receptors and enzymes of living organisms are themselves built from chiral building blocks and therefore respond selectively to one enantiomer. The two forms of carvone, for instance, smell respectively of spearmint and caraway. In pharmacology the differences can be far graver. Thalidomide, marketed in the late 1950s as a sedative and administered to pregnant women for morning sickness, caused severe birth defects in thousands of children; one enantiomer was subsequently associated with the sedative effect and the other with the harm. The case is frequently cited as an argument for producing single-enantiomer drugs, although in the case of thalidomide this would not have sufficed, since the molecule converts from one form into the other within the body.

The tragedy nonetheless prompted stricter testing regulations and stimulated the development of asymmetric synthesis, by which chemists produce predominantly one enantiomer instead of an equal mixture. Methods based on chiral catalysts were recognised with Nobel Prizes in 2001 and 2021, and today a considerable proportion of newly approved drugs are marketed as single enantiomers.

title: Taking Plastics Apart
text:
Most plastic recycling today is mechanical. Waste is sorted, washed, shredded and melted, and the material is formed into new products. This method is relatively cheap, but it has clear limits. Each time a plastic is melted, its long polymer chains tend to break, which reduces the quality of the material. Mixed or dirty waste is difficult to process, and coloured plastics cannot easily be turned into clear ones. As a result, much recycled plastic ends up in lower-value products, a process sometimes called downcycling.

Chemical recycling tries to solve this problem by breaking polymers down into smaller molecules. In pyrolysis, plastic waste is heated to several hundred degrees in the absence of oxygen, producing an oil that can be used as a raw material in refineries. In depolymerisation, certain plastics, such as PET used in drinks bottles, are broken down into their original building blocks, called monomers. These can then be purified and joined together again to make new plastic of the same quality as the original.

Critics point out that chemical recycling usually consumes a lot of energy and that some plants have turned much of their product into fuel, which is burned rather than made into new plastic. Supporters reply that the technology can handle waste that mechanical recycling cannot. Recently, scientists have also discovered enzymes that can break down PET at moderate temperatures, and companies are testing them at larger scales.

title: Pulling Carbon from the Sky
text:
Whereas capturing carbon dioxide from the flue gas of a power station or a cement kiln is technically demanding, extracting it directly from the atmosphere is considerably harder still. The difficulty is essentially one of dilution: flue gases may contain more than ten percent carbon dioxide, while ambient air contains only about 0.04 percent, so that enormous volumes of air must be brought into contact with a capturing agent in order to collect a meaningful quantity of gas.

Two broad families of direct air capture (DAC) technology have emerged. In the first, air is passed over a liquid solution, typically of potassium hydroxide, with which carbon dioxide reacts to form a carbonate; the carbonate is subsequently converted to calcium carbonate and heated to around 900 °C to release a concentrated stream of the gas. In the second, solid sorbents, often porous materials bearing amine groups, bind carbon dioxide at ambient conditions and release it when heated to roughly 100 °C, a temperature at which waste heat or heat pumps may suffice. In both cases, the captured gas can be compressed and injected into deep geological formations or used as a feedstock for synthetic fuels.

Since the separation of so dilute a gas is inherently energy-intensive, the climatic benefit of DAC depends decisively on the source of the energy supplied; a plant powered by fossil fuels might emit nearly as much carbon dioxide as it removes. Current costs, commonly estimated at several hundred dollars per tonne, remain far above those of most emission reductions, which has led many analysts to argue that DAC should complement, not replace, efforts to curb emissions, being reserved for residual emissions that are otherwise difficult to eliminate.

title: The Not-So-Noble Gases
text:
For many years, chemistry textbooks described helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon as 'inert gases'. Their outer electron shells are full, which makes them very stable, and early attempts to make them react with other elements all failed. Many chemists therefore assumed that these elements could not form compounds at all.

This belief was overturned in 1962 by Neil Bartlett, a chemist working in Canada. He had noticed that a powerful compound, platinum hexafluoride, was able to remove an electron from an oxygen molecule. Bartlett realised that the energy needed to remove an electron from xenon is almost the same as for oxygen. He mixed xenon with platinum hexafluoride and obtained an orange-yellow solid, the first compound of a noble gas. Within months, other researchers had produced simple compounds of xenon and fluorine.

Since then, compounds of krypton, radon and even argon have been made, although those of argon exist only under special conditions. Helium and neon, which hold their electrons most tightly, have not been found to form stable neutral compounds under ordinary conditions. Today, the group is usually called the 'noble gases', a name that suggests reluctance to react rather than complete inactivity. Bartlett's work is often cited as an example of how careful reasoning from a single observation can overturn a long-held assumption.

questions.tip: Amaç sorusunda 'belief was overturned' gibi dönüm noktası cümlesini bul; metin onun etrafında kurulur.

title: Genes That Travel Sideways
text:
In most animals and plants, genes are passed almost exclusively from parents to offspring, a process termed vertical inheritance. Bacteria, by contrast, routinely acquire genetic material from organisms that are not their ancestors, sometimes from entirely unrelated species, a phenomenon known as horizontal gene transfer. Three principal mechanisms have been identified: transformation, in which a cell takes up fragments of DNA released into its surroundings by dead cells; transduction, in which viruses that infect bacteria inadvertently carry genes from one host to the next; and conjugation, in which two cells form a direct connection through which a small circular DNA molecule, a plasmid, is transferred.

The medical significance of this capacity can hardly be overstated. Genes conferring resistance to antibiotics frequently reside on plasmids, which may carry several such genes simultaneously, so that a single conjugation event can render a previously susceptible bacterium resistant to multiple drugs at once. Consequently, resistance that arises in a harmless species in the gut or in soil may be passed on to a dangerous pathogen, thereby spreading far more rapidly than it could through mutation and vertical inheritance alone.

The heavy use of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture accelerates this process, since every treatment eliminates susceptible bacteria while sparing those that happen to carry resistance genes, which then multiply and share their plasmids further. It is for this reason that health authorities emphasise not only the development of new drugs but also the prudent use of existing ones, together with surveillance of resistance genes in hospitals, farms and wastewater, where bacteria from many sources come into close contact.

questions.q: The main idea of the passage is that ----.
options: new antibiotics can easily overcome all forms of resistance
plasmids carrying resistance genes are found exclusively in harmless species in the soil
bacteria inherit genes only from their ancestors
viruses that infect bacteria are the main cause of antibiotic resistance in hospitals
horizontal gene transfer enables antibiotic resistance to spread rapidly among bacteria
questions.explain: 1. paragraf yatay gen aktarımını, 2-3. paragraf direncin bu yolla hızla yayılmasını anlatıyor. Şık ikisini tek cümlede birleştiriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Metnin ana fikri ne? Dayanak: Metin yatay gen aktarımının antibiyotik direncinin bakteriler arasında hızla yayılmasını nasıl sağladığını anlatıyor.
why: Metinle çelişiyor: otoriteler yeni ilacın yanında dikkatli kullanımı da vurguluyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: direnç zararsız türden tehlikeli patojene geçebiliyor; 'exclusively' yanlış.
Metinle çelişiyor: bakteriler ata olmayan canlılardan da gen alır.
Virüsler üç mekanizmadan sadece biri; hastanedeki ana sebep olarak sunulmuyor.
questions.tip: Ana fikir sorusunda mekanizma ile sonucunu birleştiren şıkkı seç.

questions.q: According to the passage, a single conjugation event may make a bacterium resistant to several drugs because ----.
options: a plasmid can carry more than one resistance gene
conjugation creates new mutations in every gene
the bacterium turns into a virus that infects other cells

susceptible bacteria multiply faster after treatment
questions.explain: Metin plazmitlerin 'may carry several such genes simultaneously' olduğunu söylüyor. Şık 'several' yerine 'more than one' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Tek bir konjugasyon bakteriyi neden birçok ilaca dirençli yapabilir? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Plazmitler aynı anda birkaç direnç geni taşıyabilir.'
why: Konjugasyonun her gende mutasyon yarattığı yazmıyor; gen aktarır.

questions.tip: 'so that' kalıbından önceki kısım sebebi verir; sorunun sonucunu metinde bul, geriye oku.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that resistance genes are monitored in wastewater because ----.
options: it contains no harmless species

questions.tip: 'where' ile başlayan yan cümle bir yerin özelliğini verir; izleme sebebi o özelliktir.

title: The Crowd Inside Us
text:
The human gut is home to trillions of microorganisms, mostly bacteria, belonging to hundreds of different species. Together they are known as the gut microbiota. For a long time, they were seen mainly as passengers or as potential causes of disease. Over the past two decades, however, new methods of DNA sequencing have allowed scientists to identify microbes that cannot be grown in the laboratory, and this has revealed how important they are for our health.

Gut bacteria break down dietary fibre that human enzymes cannot digest, producing short-chain fatty acids that nourish the cells lining the colon. They help to produce certain vitamins, train the immune system and make it harder for harmful bacteria to settle in the gut. Differences in the composition of the microbiota have been linked to conditions such as obesity, diabetes and inflammatory bowel disease.

Scientists warn, however, that many of these links are correlations. Finding that people with a disease have a different microbiota does not show that the microbes caused the disease; the illness, or the drugs used to treat it, might instead have changed the microbes. Experiments in mice raised without any bacteria have provided stronger evidence in some cases, but mice are not humans. One treatment with clearly proven benefit is faecal microbiota transplantation, which is used against a severe, recurring infection caused by the bacterium Clostridioides difficile.

questions.q: According to the passage, DNA sequencing has been important in microbiota research because it ----.
options: produces short-chain fatty acids
allows the identification of microbes that cannot be grown in the laboratory
has proved that microbes cause obesity
is used to transplant bacteria from healthy people into patients suffering from obesity or diabetes
has shown that gut bacteria are mere passengers
questions.explain: Metin 'allowed scientists to identify microbes that cannot be grown in the laboratory' diyor. Şık bunu neredeyse aynı kelimelerle veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: DNA dizilemesi mikrobiyota araştırmasında neden önemli oldu? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Yeni yöntemler laboratuvarda üretilemeyen mikropları tanımlamayı sağladı.'
why: Kısa zincirli yağ asitlerini bağırsak bakterileri üretir; DNA dizilemesi değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: bunlar korelasyon; neden olduğu kanıtlanmadı.
Nakil bir tedavi yöntemi; dizileme ile karıştırıyor. Ayrıca obeziteye değil enfeksiyona uygulanıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: dizileme bakterilerin önemli olduğunu gösterdi.
questions.tip: 'allowed scientists to' kalıbı bir yöntemin katkısını verir; soru katkıyı soruyorsa o fiili ara.

questions.q: The author points out that many links between the microbiota and disease are correlations in order to ----.
options: suggest that drugs never affect gut bacteria
show that faecal transplantation is ineffective
argue that experiments on mice are unnecessary
warn that such findings do not necessarily show cause and effect
prove that changes in the microbes are the main cause of diabetes
questions.explain: Metin 'does not show that the microbes caused the disease' diyor. Şık bunu 'do not necessarily show cause and effect' ile söylüyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazar birçok bağın korelasyon olduğunu neden vurguluyor? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Hastalarda farklı mikrobiyota bulmak mikropların hastalığa yol açtığını göstermez.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: yazar ilaçların mikropları değiştirmiş olabileceğini söylüyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: dışkı nakli kanıtlanmış faydalı bir tedavi.

questions.tip: Metinde 'warn' fiili varsa yazarın amacı 'uyarmak'tır; şıkta da 'warn' arayabilirsin.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that faecal microbiota transplantation ----.
options: differs from many proposed microbiota links in having clearly proven benefit
was first tested on people who had been raised entirely without any bacteria
causes infections by Clostridioides difficile
has no proven medical use
is used mainly to treat obesity
questions.explain: Paragraf diğer bağların sadece korelasyon olduğunu söylüyor, sonra nakli 'clearly proven benefit' olarak ayırıyor. Şık bu farkı veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Dışkı mikrobiyota nakli hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (son cümle): 'Faydası açıkça kanıtlanmış bir tedavi dışkı mikrobiyota naklidir.'
why: Bakterisiz büyütülen olanlar fareler; insanlar değil.

title: The Caps on Our Chromosomes
text:
At the ends of every human chromosome lie telomeres, stretches of a short DNA sequence repeated thousands of times, which protect the genetic material in a manner often likened to the plastic tips that keep shoelaces from fraying. Because the enzymes that copy DNA cannot replicate the very end of a linear molecule, a small portion of each telomere is lost whenever a cell divides. When telomeres become critically short, the cell ceases dividing and enters a state termed senescence, or dies.

This progressive shortening was proposed in the 1970s as an explanation for the observation, made by Leonard Hayflick, that normal human cells grown in culture divide only a limited number of times. Certain cells, however, including stem cells and germ cells, express telomerase, an enzyme that adds the repeated sequence back to chromosome ends; its discovery by Elizabeth Blackburn and Carol Greider was recognised, together with work by Jack Szostak, with the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

It might be supposed that activating telomerase throughout the body would postpone ageing, yet the matter is complicated by the fact that the great majority of cancers reactivate telomerase, thereby acquiring the capacity to divide indefinitely. Limited telomere length may thus serve as a barrier against tumour growth, so that the mechanism which contributes to the decline of tissues in old age simultaneously protects the young organism from cancer. Moreover, although shorter telomeres are statistically associated with age-related diseases, telomere length varies considerably among individuals of the same age, which limits its usefulness as a measure of biological age.

questions.q: According to the passage, telomeres become shorter with each cell division because ----.
options: the plastic tips of chromosomes fray over time
the enzymes that copy DNA cannot replicate the very end of a linear molecule
stem cells consume the repeated sequences
telomerase removes a small part of the repeated sequence whenever the cell divides
cancer cells attack the ends of chromosomes
questions.explain: Metin 'Because the enzymes that copy DNA cannot replicate the very end of a linear molecule' diyor. Şık bu cümleyi aynen veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Telomerler her bölünmede neden kısalır? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'DNA'yı kopyalayan enzimler doğrusal molekülün en ucunu kopyalayamadığı için her bölünmede bir kısmı kaybolur.'
why: Plastik uç sadece bir benzetme; kromozomlarda plastik yok.
Kök hücreler diziyi tüketmez; tersine telomeraz ile ekler.
Ters bilgi: telomeraz diziyi ekler, çıkarmaz.
Kanser hücreleri telomerazı yeniden çalıştırır; uçlara saldırmaz.
questions.tip: Benzetmeyi ('likened to') gerçek bilgi sanma; sebep 'Because' ile verilen cümlededir.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that activating telomerase throughout the body ----.
options: could carry the risk of making it easier for tumours to grow
would make telomere length identical among individuals
has been shown to prevent all age-related diseases
is impossible because no human cells express telomerase
would cause cells to enter senescence earlier
questions.explain: Kısa telomer tümörü sınırlıyorsa, telomerazı her yerde açmak bu engeli kaldırır. Şık bunu 'carry the risk of making it easier for tumours to grow' diye veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Telomerazı tüm vücutta çalıştırmak hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Kanserlerin büyük çoğunluğu telomerazı yeniden çalıştırır; sınırlı telomer uzunluğu tümöre karşı bir engel olabilir.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: telomer uzunluğu kişiden kişiye çok değişir; eşit olacağı yazmıyor.
Böyle bir şey kanıtlanmadı; metin konunun karmaşık olduğunu söylüyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: kök hücre ve üreme hücreleri telomeraz üretir.
Ters bilgi: telomeraz telomeri uzatır, hücre yaşlanmasını geciktirir.
questions.tip: 'It might be supposed ..., yet' kalıbı beklenen fikri çürütür; cevap 'yet' sonrasındadır.

questions.q: The phrase 'this progressive shortening' at the beginning of the second paragraph refers to ----.
options: the shortening of the period that cells spend in culture
the decrease in telomerase activity in cancer cells

the addition of repeated sequences by telomerase
the decline in the number of stem cells with age

questions.anlam: Soru: 2. paragraf başındaki 'this progressive shortening' neyi gösteriyor? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Hücre her bölündüğünde her telomerin küçük bir kısmı kaybolur.'
why: Kültürde geçen süre kısalmıyor; bölünme sayısı sınırlı.
Kanser hücrelerinde telomeraz azalmaz, yeniden çalışır; ayrıca bu sonra geliyor.
Ters bilgi: telomeraz diziyi ekler; bu kısalma değil uzama.
Kök hücre sayısının azalması metinde yok.
questions.tip: 'This + isim' bir önceki paragrafın ana sürecini gösterir; isimdeki kelimeyle ('shortening') eşleştir.

title: Clocks in Every Cell
text:
Almost all living things, from bacteria to humans, show daily rhythms in their behaviour and body functions. In humans, body temperature, hormone levels, blood pressure and alertness all rise and fall over a period of roughly 24 hours. These are called circadian rhythms, from the Latin 'circa diem', meaning 'about a day'. Importantly, they continue even when people are kept in constant light or darkness, which shows that they are produced by an internal clock rather than simply by the environment.

In the 1980s and 1990s, researchers studying fruit flies identified the genes behind this clock. One gene, named 'period', produces a protein that builds up in the cell during the night and then blocks the activity of its own gene. As the protein is slowly broken down, the gene becomes active again, and the cycle starts once more. This feedback loop takes about 24 hours. For this discovery, Jeffrey Hall, Michael Rosbash and Michael Young received the Nobel Prize in 2017.

In mammals, a master clock in the brain is reset every day by light entering the eyes, and it coordinates smaller clocks in organs such as the liver. When the internal clock and the external environment do not match, as in jet lag or night-shift work, people often feel tired and unwell. Long-term disruption has been linked to a higher risk of metabolic and heart problems.

questions.q: According to the passage, the fact that circadian rhythms continue in constant darkness shows that ----.
options: they exist only in fruit flies
they last exactly 24 hours in all organisms
darkness speeds up the body's clock
they are generated by an internal clock
they are caused entirely by changes in light
questions.explain: Metin 'they are produced by an internal clock rather than simply by the environment' diyor. Şık 'produced' yerine 'generated' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Ritimlerin sürekli karanlıkta devam etmesi neyi gösterir? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Bu, ritimlerin sadece çevre tarafından değil, iç bir saat tarafından üretildiğini gösterir.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: ritimler bakteriden insana hemen tüm canlılarda var.
Metin 'roughly 24 hours' diyor; 'exactly ... all' aşırı genelleme.
Karanlığın saati hızlandırdığı metinde yok.
Metinle çelişiyor: ritimler sadece ışıkla açıklanmaz.
questions.tip: 'which shows that' kalıbından sonrasını oku; 'gösterir' sorusunun cevabı oradadır.

questions.q: The phrase 'its own gene' in the second paragraph refers to ----.
options: the clock in the liver
a gene found only in mammals

the period gene
questions.explain: 'its' proteini, 'its own gene' de bu proteini üreten geni, yani 'period' genini gösterir. Bu bir geri besleme döngüsüdür.
questions.anlam: Soru: 2. paragraftaki 'its own gene' neyi gösteriyor? Dayanak (2. paragraf): ''period' geni bir protein üretir; protein gece birikir ve kendi geninin etkinliğini engeller.'
why: Karaciğerdeki saat 3. paragrafta geçiyor; ilgisi yok.

why: Meyve sinekleri sadece genlerin bulunduğu deney hayvanı; uykuları anlatılmıyor.

title: Fewer Wings
text:
In 2017, a study from Germany attracted worldwide attention. Volunteers had collected flying insects in traps in nature reserves for 27 years, and when the samples were weighed, the total mass of insects caught had fallen by about three quarters. Since then, studies in other regions have reported declines in many insect groups, although the picture is not the same everywhere, and some species have become more common.

The reasons are thought to be several and to act together. Loss of habitat, as meadows and hedgerows are replaced by intensive farmland and buildings, removes the plants that insects feed on. Pesticides, including a group called neonicotinoids, can harm insects that were not their intended targets. Artificial light at night attracts and disorients many night-flying species, and climate change shifts the conditions to which species are adapted.

These declines matter because insects play central roles in ecosystems. Around three quarters of the main types of food crops benefit to some degree from animal pollination, mainly by insects. Insects also break down dead plants and animals, and they are food for many birds, bats and fish. Scientists stress that long-term data are still scarce in many parts of the world, especially in the tropics, where most insect species live. They therefore call for more systematic monitoring, while also recommending practical measures such as leaving strips of wild flowers along fields and reducing unnecessary use of pesticides.

options: the benefits of artificial light for night-flying insects
why some insect species have become more common
the methods used by German volunteers to weigh birds
the role of bats in pollinating food crops
evidence of insect decline, its likely causes and why it matters
questions.explain: 1. paragraf kanıt, 2. paragraf sebepler, 3. paragraf önemi anlatıyor. Şık üçünü 'evidence ..., its likely causes and why it matters' ile kapsıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Metin esas olarak neyi tartışıyor? Dayanak: Metin böcek azalmasının kanıtlarını, olası sebeplerini ve neden önemli olduğunu anlatıyor.
why: Metinle çelişiyor: yapay ışık gece uçan böcekleri yönünü şaşırtır.
Bazı türlerin artması sadece kısa bir not.

questions.tip: Ana fikir sorusunda paragraf sırasıyla eşleşen üç parçalı şıkkı ara.

questions.q: According to the passage, the German study published in 2017 ----.

why: Metinle çelişiyor: tablo her yerde aynı değil.
Çalışma Almanya'da gönüllüler tarafından yapıldı; tropiklerde değil.

title: Cities That Trap Heat
text:
On a calm summer evening, the centre of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside. This effect, known as the urban heat island, was first described in the early nineteenth century by Luke Howard, who compared temperatures in London with those outside the city.

Several factors contribute to the effect. Materials such as asphalt, concrete and brick absorb a large part of the sunlight that falls on them and store heat during the day, releasing it slowly at night. Cities also have fewer trees and less open soil, so less water evaporates; since evaporation uses energy, this natural cooling is reduced. Tall buildings trap heat between them and slow the wind, while cars, factories and air conditioners add waste heat directly to the air.

The urban heat island is more than an inconvenience. During heatwaves, high night-time temperatures prevent the body from recovering, which increases the risk of illness and death, especially among elderly people. Higher temperatures also increase demand for air conditioning, which in turn produces more waste heat and, where electricity comes from fossil fuels, more greenhouse gases.

Cities are responding in various ways. Planting trees provides shade and cooling through evaporation. Light-coloured 'cool roofs' and pavements reflect more sunlight, and green roofs covered with plants can lower roof temperatures considerably. Some cities also protect corridors of open space that allow cooler air from the countryside to flow into the centre.

questions.q: According to the passage, having fewer trees and less open soil makes cities warmer because ----.
options: open soil absorbs far more sunlight than asphalt and concrete do
evaporation adds waste heat to the air
trees release stored heat at night
open spaces slow the wind
less cooling takes place through the evaporation of water
questions.explain: Metin 'less water evaporates; since evaporation uses energy, this natural cooling is reduced' diyor. Şık bunu 'less cooling takes place through the evaporation of water' ile veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Az ağaç ve az açık toprak şehirleri neden ısıtır? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Daha az su buharlaşır; buharlaşma enerji kullandığı için bu doğal soğuma azalır.'
why: Metinde açık toprağın asfalttan çok ışık emdiği yazmıyor.
Ters bilgi: buharlaşma enerji kullanır yani soğutur; atık ısı arabalardan gelir.
Gece ısı veren malzemeler asfalt ve betondur; ağaçlar değil.
Rüzgârı yavaşlatan yüksek binalardır; açık alanlar değil.
questions.tip: 'since' kelimesi 'çünkü' demektir; 'since' ile başlayan kısım sebebi verir.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that the use of air conditioning during heatwaves ----.
options: was first described by Luke Howard
can make the heat island effect worse
eliminates the risk of illness for elderly people
reduces waste heat in city centres
has no connection with greenhouse gas emissions
questions.explain: Klima daha fazla atık ısı üretiyor ve atık ısı ısı adasının sebeplerinden biri. Şık bunu 'can make the heat island effect worse' diye çıkarıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Sıcak hava dalgasında klima kullanımı hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Klima talebi artar, bu da daha fazla atık ısı ve sera gazı üretir.'
why: Luke Howard ısı adasını tanımladı; klimayı değil.
Klima riski ortadan kaldırmaz; metinde böyle bir şey yok.
Ters bilgi: klima atık ısıyı artırır.
Metinle çelişiyor: elektrik fosil yakıttan gelirse daha fazla sera gazı çıkar.
questions.tip: 'which in turn' bir zincir kurar; zincirin sonunu sorunun başıyla birleştir.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a way in which cities are responding to the problem?
options: building taller structures to block sunlight
planting trees
using light-coloured roofs and pavements
covering roofs with plants
protecting corridors of open space
questions.explain: Metinde yüksek binalar sorunun sebebi olarak geçiyor (ısıyı hapseder, rüzgârı yavaşlatır); çözüm olarak değil. Diğer dört şık 4. paragrafta açıkça var.
questions.anlam: Soru: Hangisi şehirlerin verdiği tepkilerden biri olarak SÖZ EDİLMİYOR? Dayanak (4. paragraf): Ağaç dikmek, açık renkli çatılar, yeşil çatılar ve açık alan koridorları sayılıyor.
why: Bu 4. paragrafta ilk çözüm olarak geçiyor.
Bu 4. paragrafta 'cool roofs' olarak geçiyor.
Bu 4. paragrafta yeşil çatılar olarak geçiyor.
Bu 4. paragrafın son cümlesinde geçiyor.
questions.tip: 'NOT' sorusunda çözüm paragrafını şık şık işaretle; sorunun sebebi olarak geçen şeyi seç.

title: Where the Oxygen Runs Out
text:
Each summer, an area of the Gulf of Mexico that in some years exceeds 15,000 square kilometres becomes so depleted of oxygen near the seabed that fish flee and less mobile organisms such as worms and clams suffocate. Such hypoxic regions, popularly known as dead zones, have been documented in several hundred coastal areas worldwide, and their number has risen markedly since the mid-twentieth century.

The principal cause is eutrophication, the over-enrichment of water with nutrients, chiefly nitrogen and phosphorus, much of which is washed from fertilised farmland into rivers and ultimately into the sea, while sewage contributes further quantities. These nutrients stimulate explosive growth of phytoplankton near the surface. When the algae die, they sink and are decomposed by bacteria, which consume dissolved oxygen in the process. Where the water column is stratified, with warmer, fresher water lying above colder, saltier water, the oxygen consumed at depth cannot readily be replenished from the surface, and hypoxia develops.

Climate change is likely to exacerbate the problem, since warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen and tends to strengthen stratification, whereas heavier rainfall in some regions may increase nutrient runoff. Notwithstanding this bleak outlook, dead zones are not necessarily irreversible. The Black Sea's north-western shelf, which suffered severe hypoxia in the 1970s and 1980s, partially recovered during the 1990s after the collapse of the Soviet economy led to a steep decline in fertiliser use in the surrounding countries. The episode, though hardly a model for policy, demonstrated that reducing nutrient inputs can allow oxygen levels to recover within years rather than centuries.

questions.q: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: The Gulf of Mexico has the only dead zone that has been documented.
Dead zones are caused mainly by nutrient pollution and can recover if nutrient inputs fall.
The collapse of the Soviet economy proved to be an ideal model for environmental policy in the Black Sea.
Phytoplankton remove oxygen directly from the seabed by sinking.
Climate change will make dead zones disappear.
questions.explain: 2. paragraf ana sebebi 'eutrophication' olarak veriyor, 3. paragraf 'reducing nutrient inputs can allow oxygen levels to recover' diyor. Şık sebep ve çözümü birlikte veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Metnin ana fikrini en iyi hangisi ifade eder? Dayanak: Ölü bölgeler esas olarak besin kirliliğinden (ötrofikasyon) kaynaklanır; Karadeniz örneği besin girdisi azalınca toparlanabildiklerini gösterir.
why: Metinle çelişiyor: dünyada birkaç yüz kıyı bölgesinde ölü bölge var.
Metinle çelişiyor: yazar bunu 'hardly a model for policy' diye niteliyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: oksijeni tüketen, ölü algleri parçalayan bakterilerdir.
Metinle çelişiyor: iklim değişikliği sorunu büyütecek.
questions.tip: Ana fikir şıkkı hem sebebi hem sonucu taşımalı; tek örneğe (Karadeniz) dayanan şıklar eksiktir.

questions.q: According to the passage, stratification contributes to hypoxia because ----.
options: it makes deep water warmer than surface water
it stimulates bacteria to produce oxygen
it prevents oxygen consumed at depth from being replenished from the surface
it increases the amount of nitrogen and phosphorus that rivers carry into the sea
it causes dead algae to remain at the surface
questions.explain: Metin 'the oxygen consumed at depth cannot readily be replenished from the surface' diyor. Şık 'cannot be replenished' yerine 'prevents ... from being replenished' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Tabakalaşma hipoksiye neden katkıda bulunur? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Su tabakalıysa derinde tüketilen oksijen yüzeyden kolayca yenilenemez.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: sıcak su üstte, soğuk su altta.
Metinle çelişiyor: bakteriler oksijen tüketir, üretmez.
Besin miktarını tarım ve kanalizasyon artırır; tabakalaşma değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: ölü algler dibe çöker.
questions.tip: 'Where ...' ile başlayan koşul cümlesinin ikinci yarısı sonucu ve sebebi verir.

questions.q: The author refers to the Black Sea in order to ----.
options: illustrate how heavier rainfall in some regions increases the nutrient runoff from farmland
recommend economic collapse as a solution to pollution
compare the size of the Black Sea with the Gulf of Mexico
show that dead zones can recover relatively quickly once nutrient inputs are reduced
prove that the Black Sea has never experienced hypoxia
questions.explain: Yazar 'dead zones are not necessarily irreversible' deyip Karadeniz'i örnek veriyor. Şık 'within years rather than centuries' kısmını 'relatively quickly' diye veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazar Karadeniz'den neden söz ediyor? Dayanak (son cümle): 'Bu olay besin girdisini azaltmanın oksijenin yüzyıllar değil yıllar içinde toparlanmasını sağlayabildiğini gösterdi.'
why: Yağış artışı ayrı bir cümlede; Karadeniz örneğiyle ilgili değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: yazar bunu politika modeli olarak görmüyor.
Boyut karşılaştırması yapılmıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: Karadeniz 1970-80'lerde ciddi hipoksi yaşadı.
questions.tip: 'Notwithstanding' ile başlayan cümleden sonraki örnek, o cümlenin iddiasını kanıtlar.

title: Wetlands That Hold Carbon
text:
Peatlands, wetlands in which waterlogged conditions prevent dead plant material from fully decomposing, cover only around three percent of the Earth's land surface; nevertheless, they are estimated to store roughly a third of all soil carbon, which is more than is held in the vegetation of all the world's forests combined. This disproportion arises because peat accumulates extremely slowly, often by about a millimetre a year, over thousands of years, the lack of oxygen in saturated soil inhibiting the microbes that would otherwise break the material down.

Because the carbon is locked away only so long as the peat remains wet, the drainage of peatlands for agriculture, forestry or peat extraction has consequences that are disproportionate to the area affected. Once the water table is lowered, oxygen penetrates the peat, decomposition resumes and carbon dioxide is released, a process that can continue for decades. Drained peat is moreover highly flammable; in 2015, fires in drained peatlands in Indonesia burned for weeks, producing smoke that spread across Southeast Asia and causing emissions that on some days exceeded those of the entire US economy.

Rewetting, which involves blocking drainage ditches so as to raise the water table, can halt much of this loss, and it has been undertaken on a large scale in countries such as Germany and the United Kingdom. Rewetting is not, however, without complications: it may temporarily increase emissions of methane, a more potent but shorter-lived greenhouse gas, and it usually ends conventional farming on the land. Even so, most studies conclude that over a period of decades the climatic benefit clearly outweighs these drawbacks.

questions.q: According to the passage, peatlands store large amounts of carbon because ----.
options: they are regularly burned to release methane
they cover a larger area than the world's forests
oxygen penetrates the saturated soil and greatly stimulates plant growth
waterlogged conditions slow the microbial breakdown of plant material
peat accumulates by several centimetres each year
questions.explain: Metin 'waterlogged conditions prevent dead plant material from fully decomposing' ve oksijensizliğin mikropları 'inhibiting' ettiğini söylüyor. Şık bunu 'slow the microbial breakdown' ile veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Turbalıklar neden büyük miktarda karbon depolar? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Suya doymuş toprakta oksijen eksikliği, malzemeyi parçalayacak mikropları engeller.'
why: Yanma kurutulmuş turbalıkların sorunu; karbon depolamanın sebebi değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: turbalıklar karanın sadece yüzde 3'ünü kaplar.
Metinle çelişiyor: oksijen girerse çürüme başlar.
Metinle çelişiyor: turba yılda yaklaşık bir milimetre birikir.
questions.tip: Cümlede virgülle eklenen 'the lack of oxygen ... inhibiting' gibi kısımlar sebebi verir; atlama.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that a drained peatland ----.
options: may go on emitting carbon dioxide long after it has been drained
stops releasing carbon as soon as the water table falls
stores more carbon than an undrained peatland
produces more methane than a rewetted one
is less likely to catch fire than a wet one
questions.explain: Metin 'a process that can continue for decades' diyor. Şık bunu 'may go on emitting carbon dioxide long after it has been drained' diye veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Kurutulmuş turbalık hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Su seviyesi düşünce çürüme yeniden başlar ve CO2 salınır; bu süreç onlarca yıl sürebilir.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: su seviyesi düşünce salım başlar.
Metinle çelişiyor: kurutma depolanan karbonu salar.
Metan geçici olarak yeniden ıslatmada artar; kurutulmuşla karşılaştırma ters.
Metinle çelişiyor: kurutulmuş turba çok yanıcıdır.
questions.tip: 'can continue for decades' gibi süre ifadesi şıkta 'long after' olarak karşına çıkar.

questions.q: The author's view of rewetting can best be described as ----.
options: enthusiastic, claiming that it has no drawbacks
supportive, while acknowledging some disadvantages
doubtful, as it has never been tried on a large scale
strongly opposed, because it raises methane emissions permanently
neutral, since no studies have assessed it
questions.explain: Yazar dezavantajları ('not without complications') sayıp 'the climatic benefit clearly outweighs these drawbacks' diyor. Bu, dezavantajları kabul eden destekçi bir tutum.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazarın yeniden ıslatmaya bakışı nasıl? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Metanı geçici artırabilir ve tarımı bitirir... Yine de çoğu çalışma iklim faydasının bu dezavantajlardan açıkça ağır bastığını söylüyor.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: yazar dezavantajları açıkça sayıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: Almanya ve İngiltere'de büyük ölçekte uygulandı.
Metinle çelişiyor: metan artışı geçici (temporarily).
Metinle çelişiyor: çoğu çalışma konuyu değerlendirdi.
questions.tip: 'not without ...; even so ...' yapısı 'olumlu ama sorunları kabul eden' bir tutumu gösterir.

title: Lighthouses in Space
text:
In 1967, Jocelyn Bell, then a graduate student at Cambridge, noticed an unusual pattern in the data from a radio telescope she had helped to construct: a series of pulses arriving every 1.34 seconds with a regularity that seemed almost artificial, so much so that the source was half-jokingly labelled 'LGM-1', for 'little green men'. The discovery of further sources of this kind in other parts of the sky soon ruled out an extraterrestrial civilisation, and the objects, named pulsars, were identified as rapidly rotating neutron stars.

A neutron star is the collapsed core left behind when a massive star explodes as a supernova. Into a sphere perhaps twenty kilometres across is compressed more mass than that of the Sun, so that a teaspoonful of its material would weigh hundreds of millions of tonnes. Since angular momentum is conserved as the core contracts, the star spins extremely fast, while its magnetic field is intensified enormously. Beams of radiation emitted from the magnetic poles sweep across space as the star rotates, and an observer whose line of sight the beam crosses detects a pulse once per rotation, in much the same way as a ship perceives a lighthouse.

Pulsars have since proved to be extraordinarily useful natural instruments. The steadiest of them rival atomic clocks in precision, which has enabled astronomers to detect planets orbiting a pulsar and to test general relativity. The 1974 Nobel Prize in Physics, notably, went to her supervisor, Antony Hewish, and to Martin Ryle, an omission that has been widely debated; Bell Burnell, as she later became, received a major physics prize in 2018 and donated the money to support under-represented students.

questions.q: According to the passage, the idea that the signals came from an extraterrestrial civilisation was abandoned because ----.
options: neutron stars were known to send messages
the radio telescope was found to be faulty
the pulses stopped after 1.34 seconds
Antony Hewish proved that the pulses were artificial
similar sources were found in other parts of the sky
questions.explain: Metin 'The discovery of further sources of this kind in other parts of the sky soon ruled out' diyor. Şık 'further sources of this kind' yerine 'similar sources' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Sinyallerin dünya dışı bir uygarlıktan geldiği fikri neden bırakıldı? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Gökyüzünün başka yerlerinde benzer kaynakların bulunması bu fikri kısa sürede eledi.'
why: Nötron yıldızlarının mesaj gönderdiği yazmıyor; bu mantıksız.
Teleskopun arızalı olduğu metinde yok.
1,34 saniye atımlar arasındaki süre; atımlar durmadı.
Hewish'in atımların yapay olduğunu kanıtladığı yazmıyor; tersine doğal oldukları anlaşıldı.
questions.tip: 'ruled out' (eledi) fiilini bul; öznesi olan isim sebebi verir.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that an observer would NOT detect pulses from a pulsar if ----.
options: the star rotated more rapidly
its magnetic field were intensified enormously as the core contracted
it were smaller than twenty kilometres across
its beams never crossed the observer's line of sight
it had formed in a supernova explosion
questions.explain: Atım sadece ışın görüş hattından geçtiğinde algılanır. Işın hiç geçmezse atım da algılanmaz; şık bunu söylüyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Gözlemci bir pulsarın atımlarını hangi durumda ALGILAMAZ? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Işının görüş hattını kestiği bir gözlemci her dönüşte bir atım algılar.'
why: Metin atım algılamayı ışının gözlemcinin görüş hattını kesmesine bağlıyor; dönüş hızı bu şart olarak geçmiyor.
Güçlü manyetik alan ışınların oluşmasına katkıdır; engel değil.
Boyut algılamayı etkilemiyor; metinde böyle bir koşul yok.
Metne göre nötron yıldızları zaten süpernova patlamasıyla oluşur; bu durum atımın algılanmasını engellemez.
questions.tip: Koşul sorusunda metindeki 'whose line of sight the beam crosses' koşulunu bul ve tersini al.

questions.q: In the last paragraph, the author implies that Bell's exclusion from the 1974 Nobel Prize ----.
options: was fully justified because she was only a student
led directly to the discovery of planets orbiting pulsars
has been regarded by many as questionable
was the reason why Ryle shared the prize
was corrected when she received the Nobel Prize in 2018
questions.explain: Metin bunu 'an omission that has been widely debated' diye anlatıyor. Şık 'widely debated' yerine 'regarded by many as questionable' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Yazar son paragrafta Bell'in 1974 Nobel'inden dışlanması hakkında ne ima ediyor? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Ödül danışmanı Hewish'e ve Ryle'a gitti; bu ihmal geniş çapta tartışıldı.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: 'omission' ve 'debated' kelimeleri haklı görülmediğini gösterir.
Pulsar çevresindeki gezegenler kararlı pulsarlar sayesinde bulundu; ödülle ilgisi yok.
Ryle'ın ödülü paylaşma sebebi metinde açıklanmıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: 2018'de aldığı Nobel değil, başka büyük bir fizik ödülüydü.
questions.tip: İma sorusunda yazarın seçtiği kelimelere bak: 'omission, debated' eleştiri içerir.

title: The Oldest Light
text:
In 1964, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson, two radio astronomers at Bell Laboratories in New Jersey, were troubled by a faint, persistent hiss in their antenna that appeared to come uniformly from every direction in the sky. Having eliminated every plausible source of interference, including, famously, the droppings of pigeons nesting inside the instrument, they learned that physicists at nearby Princeton had predicted exactly such a signal as a relic of a hot, dense early universe.

According to the Big Bang model, the universe was for its first 380,000 years or so a plasma of charged particles so dense that light could not travel far without being scattered. When expansion had cooled it to about 3,000 degrees, electrons combined with nuclei to form neutral atoms, whereupon the universe became transparent and the light then present was released. Stretched by the subsequent expansion of space, that radiation now reaches us as microwaves corresponding to a temperature of only 2.7 degrees above absolute zero; hence its name, the cosmic microwave background (CMB).

The discovery, for which Penzias and Wilson shared the 1978 Nobel Prize, persuaded most cosmologists to abandon the rival steady-state theory, which had no natural way to account for such radiation. Subsequent satellites, notably COBE, WMAP and Planck, revealed that the background is not perfectly uniform but contains minute fluctuations of about one part in 100,000. These variations, far from being mere noise, record the slight differences in density from which galaxies later grew, and their detailed statistics have enabled cosmologists to estimate the age of the universe, at about 13.8 billion years, with remarkable precision.

questions.q: Which of the following would be the most appropriate title for the passage?
options: Echoes of the Early Universe
Pigeons and Radio Antennas
The Triumph of the Steady-State Theory
How Galaxies Destroy Microwaves
Building Satellites at Bell Laboratories
questions.explain: Metin Büyük Patlama'dan kalan ışığın bulunuşunu ve önemini anlatıyor. 'Echoes of the Early Universe' (erken evrenin yankıları) bunu karşılıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Metin için en uygun başlık hangisi? Dayanak: Metin evrenin ilk dönemlerinden kalan ışığı, yani kozmik mikrodalga arka plan ışımasını anlatıyor.
why: Güvercinler sadece eğlenceli bir detay.
Metinle çelişiyor: keşif kararlı durum teorisini zayıflattı.
Galaksilerin mikrodalgayı yok ettiği metinde yok.
Bell Laboratuvarı'nda uydu yapılmadı; uydular sonraki görevler.
questions.tip: Başlık sorusunda detay olarak geçen eğlenceli bilgiler (güvercin) tuzaktır; ana kavramı seç.

questions.q: According to the passage, the early universe became transparent when ----.
options: galaxies grew from differences in density
its temperature rose to about 3,000 degrees as a result of expansion
electrons combined with nuclei to form neutral atoms
light was stretched into microwaves
the steady-state theory was abandoned
questions.explain: Metin 'electrons combined with nuclei to form neutral atoms, whereupon the universe became transparent' diyor. Şık bunu aynen veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Erken evren ne zaman şeffaf hâle geldi? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Elektronlar çekirdeklerle birleşip nötr atomlar oluşturduğunda evren şeffaflaştı.'
why: Galaksiler çok sonra oluştu; şeffaflıkla ilgisi yok.
Metinle çelişiyor: genişleme evreni soğuttu, ısıtmadı.
Işığın mikrodalgaya uzaması sonradan oldu.
Teorinin terk edilmesi 1960'larda bilim tarihinde oldu; evrenin olayı değil.
questions.tip: 'whereupon' (bunun üzerine) kelimesi iki olayı sıraya koyar; ondan önceki olay cevaptır.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that the steady-state theory ----.
options: predicted the minute fluctuations measured by Planck
was weakened because it could not readily explain the CMB
was proposed by Penzias and Wilson
remains the most widely accepted cosmological model
explains why the universe is 13.8 billion years old
questions.explain: Metin teorinin 'had no natural way to account for such radiation' olduğunu söylüyor. Şık 'account for' yerine 'explain', 'abandon' yerine 'weakened' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Kararlı durum teorisi hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Keşif kozmologları böyle bir ışımayı açıklamanın doğal bir yolu olmayan rakip teoriyi bırakmaya ikna etti.'
why: Dalgalanmaları Planck ölçtü; bu teori onları öngörmedi.
Penzias ve Wilson ışımayı buldu; bu teoriyi önermediler.
Metinle çelişiyor: çoğu kozmolog bu teoriyi bıraktı.
Evrenin yaşını CMB istatistikleri verdi; bu teori değil.
questions.tip: 'rival' (rakip) kelimesi bir teorinin karşı tarafta olduğunu gösterir; sonucu ona göre çıkar.

title: Nudging an Asteroid
text:
Most asteroids that cross Earth's orbit are small and harmless, but a large impact could cause destruction on a regional or even global scale. For this reason, space agencies track near-Earth objects and study ways to change their path if one were found to be on a collision course. One method, called kinetic impact, is simply to hit the asteroid with a spacecraft at high speed.

In 2022, NASA tested this idea with its Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART). The target was Dimorphos, a small asteroid about 160 metres across that orbits a larger asteroid, Didymos. Neither of them posed any threat to Earth. A binary system was chosen because a change in Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos could be measured precisely with telescopes on Earth, by timing how the two bodies passed in front of each other.

On 26 September 2022, the spacecraft struck Dimorphos at about 6 kilometres per second. Before the impact, Dimorphos took 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit Didymos; afterwards, the period was about 32 minutes shorter, far more than the minimum change of 73 seconds that had been set as a measure of success. Scientists believe that the large amount of rock thrown off by the impact pushed the asteroid further, like the recoil of a gun.

The result shows that kinetic impact can work, but only if a dangerous asteroid is discovered years in advance, since even a small push needs time to change its path enough to miss Earth.

questions.q: According to the passage, a binary asteroid system was chosen for DART because ----.
options: binary systems are the most dangerous type of asteroid that crosses Earth's orbit
Dimorphos was on a collision course with Earth
a change in the smaller asteroid's orbit could be measured accurately from Earth
the spacecraft needed two targets to succeed
Didymos was too large to be observed precisely with telescopes on Earth
questions.explain: Metin 'a change in Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos could be measured precisely' diyor. Şık 'precisely' yerine 'accurately' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: DART için neden ikili bir asteroit sistemi seçildi? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Dimorphos'un Didymos çevresindeki yörüngesindeki değişim Dünya'daki teleskoplarla hassas ölçülebilirdi.'
why: Metinde ikili sistemlerin en tehlikeli tür olduğu yazmıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: ikisi de Dünya için tehdit değildi.
Uzay aracı sadece Dimorphos'a çarptı; iki hedef gerekmedi.
Didymos'un gözlenemeyecek kadar büyük olduğu yazmıyor.
questions.tip: 'was chosen because' sorusunda metinde 'because' kelimesini bul; seçim sebebi orada.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that the DART mission ----.
options: increased the orbital period of Dimorphos by 73 seconds
showed that rock thrown off by the impact reduced its effect
prevented an asteroid from striking Earth
exceeded the goal that had been set for it
failed to change the orbit of Dimorphos
questions.explain: Hedef en az 73 saniyelik değişimdi, sonuç yaklaşık 32 dakika oldu. Şık bunu 'exceeded the goal that had been set for it' diye veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: DART görevi hakkında ne çıkarılabilir? Dayanak (3. paragraf): 'Yörünge süresi yaklaşık 32 dakika kısaldı; başarı ölçüsü olarak belirlenen 73 saniyenin çok üstünde.'
why: İki bilgiyi karıştırıyor: 73 saniye hedefti; süre kısaldı, artmadı.
Ters bilgi: fırlayan kayalar etkiyi artırdı.
Metinle çelişiyor: Dimorphos Dünya için tehdit değildi.
Metinle çelişiyor: yörünge değişti.
questions.tip: Sayıların olduğu metinde hedef ile sonucu karşılaştır; 'far more than' aşmak demektir.

questions.q: The last paragraph suggests that ----.
options: all near-Earth asteroids will eventually hit Earth
small pushes have no effect on an asteroid's path
kinetic impact has proved to be unworkable
kinetic impact can save Earth even if an asteroid is found days before impact
early detection is essential if kinetic impact is to be useful
questions.explain: Metin 'only if a dangerous asteroid is discovered years in advance' diyor. Şık bunu 'early detection is essential' ile söylüyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Son paragraf neyi ima ediyor? Dayanak (4. paragraf): 'Kinetik çarpma ancak tehlikeli asteroit yıllar önceden bulunursa işe yarar.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: çoğu asteroit küçük ve zararsız.

title: The Year Without a Summer
text:
In April 1815, Mount Tambora on the Indonesian island of Sumbawa produced the largest volcanic eruption in recorded history. Tens of thousands of people on the surrounding islands died, either directly from the eruption or from the hunger and disease that followed. But the effects of the eruption reached much further than Indonesia.

The explosion sent enormous amounts of sulphur gas high into the stratosphere, more than 20 kilometres above the ground. There, the gas reacted with water to form tiny droplets of sulphuric acid, called aerosols, which spread around the globe. Because they reflected part of the incoming sunlight back into space, average temperatures in the Northern Hemisphere fell by around half a degree to one degree Celsius for the next year or two. Unlike ash, which falls out of the atmosphere within days or weeks, these aerosols can remain in the stratosphere for a year or more because there is no rain there to wash them out.

The following year, 1816, became known in Europe and North America as 'the year without a summer'. Snow fell in New England in June, and cold, wet weather destroyed harvests across Europe, causing food prices to rise sharply. At the time, nobody connected these events to a volcano on the other side of the world. The link was established only in the twentieth century, after scientists studied later eruptions, such as Pinatubo in 1991, and measured their cooling effect directly.

questions.q: According to the passage, volcanic aerosols remain in the stratosphere longer than ash because ----.
options: they are heavier than ash particles
they are produced more than 20 kilometres below the ground
ash is reflected back into space
they react with sunlight to form new gases
there is no rain at that height to remove them
questions.explain: Metin 'because there is no rain there to wash them out' diyor. Şık 'wash them out' yerine 'remove them' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Volkanik aerosoller stratosferde kül kadar kısa değil, neden daha uzun kalır? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Orada onları yıkayacak yağmur olmadığı için bir yıl ya da daha uzun kalabilirler.'
why: Aerosollerin külden ağır olduğu metinde yok.
Metinle çelişiyor: gaz yerin 20 km üstüne, stratosfere çıkar.
Uzaya güneş ışığını yansıtan aerosollerdir; kül değil.
Metne göre suyla tepkimeye giren kükürt gazıdır ve aerosoller bu yolla oluşur; aerosollerin güneş ışığıyla yeni gaz oluşturduğu yazmıyor.
questions.tip: 'Unlike A, B' cümlesinde B'nin sebebi 'because' ile hemen arkadan gelir.

questions.q: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.

title: Sinking Ground
text:
In parts of Mexico City, Jakarta and the Central Valley of California, the ground has subsided by several metres over the past century, in some districts at rates exceeding twenty centimetres a year. Although tectonic movement and the natural compaction of young sediments play a part, the dominant cause in each case is the excessive extraction of groundwater, which has been pumped faster than rainfall and rivers can recharge the aquifers from which it is drawn.

The mechanism depends on the nature of the sediments involved. In an aquifer composed partly of clay, the water filling the pores supports a portion of the weight of the overlying ground. When it is withdrawn, this load is transferred to the clay particles, which are pressed closer together. Whereas sand and gravel largely rebound once water levels recover, compacted clay does not, so that much of the subsidence, together with the storage capacity lost along with the pore space, is effectively permanent.

The consequences extend well beyond the inconvenience of tilted buildings. Subsidence fractures pipelines, wells and roads, alters the gradients of canals and drains, and, in coastal cities, compounds the effects of sea-level rise; parts of northern Jakarta already lie below sea level and are protected by sea walls. Indonesia's decision to relocate its capital to Borneo was justified in part by such problems. Remedies exist but are slow and politically demanding: Tokyo, which suffered severe subsidence in the early twentieth century, largely halted it after the 1960s by restricting pumping and supplying industry with surface water, an example demonstrating that the process can be arrested, though rarely reversed.

questions.q: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Sand and gravel layers are responsible for most permanent subsidence.
Subsidence can easily be reversed once pumping is restricted.
Tectonic movement, rather than the extraction of groundwater, is the main reason why coastal cities are sinking.
Jakarta has solved its subsidence problem by building sea walls.
Groundwater overuse causes largely permanent subsidence, which can be halted but rarely reversed.
questions.explain: 1. paragraf ana sebebi, 2. paragraf kalıcılığı, son cümle 'can be arrested, though rarely reversed' bilgisini veriyor. Şık üçünü birleştiriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Metnin ana fikrini en iyi hangisi ifade eder? Dayanak: Aşırı yeraltı suyu çekimi büyük ölçüde kalıcı çökmeye yol açar; süreç durdurulabilir ama nadiren geri çevrilir.
why: Metinle çelişiyor: kalıcı çökmeye kil sebep olur; kum ve çakıl geri esner.
Metinle çelişiyor: süreç durdurulabilir ama nadiren geri çevrilir.
Metinle çelişiyor: baskın sebep yeraltı suyu çekimi.
Metinle çelişiyor: duvarlar sadece koruma; sorun çözülmedi.
questions.tip: Ana fikir şıkkı metnin son cümlesindeki sonucu da (arrested, rarely reversed) taşımalı.

questions.q: According to the passage, subsidence in clay-rich aquifers is largely permanent because ----.

title: When North Becomes South
text:
Earth's magnetic field, generated by the motion of molten iron in the outer core, a process referred to as the geodynamo, has not always pointed in its present direction. When lava cools, iron-bearing minerals within it become magnetised parallel to the prevailing field, thereby preserving a record of its orientation at the time. Studies of such rocks, initiated in the early twentieth century, revealed that the polarity of the field has reversed many hundreds of times, the most recent full reversal, named after Bernard Brunhes and Motonori Matuyama, having occurred about 780,000 years ago.

These reversals subsequently furnished decisive support for plate tectonics. In the early 1960s, surveys of the ocean floor disclosed stripes of alternately normal and reversed magnetisation running parallel to mid-ocean ridges and arranged symmetrically on either side of them. The pattern was readily explained if new crust formed continuously at the ridges and spread outwards, recording each reversal like a tape recorder.

Reversals are irregular, separated by intervals ranging from tens of thousands to tens of millions of years, and the transition itself appears to take a few thousand years, during which the field weakens considerably. Since the field's strength has declined by some nine percent over the past two centuries, it is occasionally suggested that a reversal is imminent; however, the current field remains stronger than its long-term average, and such declines have frequently occurred without leading to reversal. The fossil record shows no mass extinctions coinciding with past reversals, although a weaker field would allow more energetic particles to reach the upper atmosphere, posing risks chiefly to satellites and power grids rather than to life itself.

questions.q: According to the passage, lava preserves a record of the magnetic field because ----.
options: molten iron from the outer core rises with it to the surface and keeps the original direction
its iron-bearing minerals become magnetised in the direction of the field as it cools
it weakens the field as it solidifies
it is formed only at mid-ocean ridges
it reverses its own polarity every few thousand years
questions.explain: Metin 'iron-bearing minerals within it become magnetised parallel to the prevailing field' diyor. Şık 'parallel to the prevailing field' yerine 'in the direction of the field' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Lav manyetik alanın kaydını neden korur? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Lav soğurken içindeki demirli mineraller o anki alana paralel mıknatıslanır.'

Metinde lavın alanı zayıflattığı yazmıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: lav sadece okyanus sırtlarında oluşmaz.
Kutup terslenmesi Dünya'nın alanına ait; lav kendi kutbunu değiştirmez.

title: Machines That Inspect Steel
text:
In a modern cold rolling mill or galvanizing line, steel strip may move at several hundred metres per minute. At such speeds, it is impossible for human inspectors to see every scratch, hole, inclusion or rolled-in particle on the surface. For many years, plants relied on inspectors looking at samples and at the ends of coils, so many defects were found only by the customer.

Automatic surface inspection systems solve part of this problem. High-speed cameras and special lighting are placed above and below the strip, and they record images of the entire surface. Early systems used fixed rules, for example classifying a dark spot of a certain size and shape as a particular defect. Such rules worked well for common defects, but they had difficulty with new defect types or with changes in lighting and surface appearance.

Today, many systems use deep learning, a type of artificial intelligence in which a neural network learns to recognise defects from thousands of labelled example images. This approach can achieve higher accuracy and can be retrained when new products are introduced. However, it needs large amounts of carefully labelled data, and rare but serious defects may appear in only a few images. Another difficulty is that operators may not trust a system whose decisions they cannot explain. For this reason, the systems are usually used to support quality engineers rather than to replace them, and the images they store also help engineers find the process step where a defect first appeared.

questions.q: According to the passage, early rule-based inspection systems ----.

questions.anlam: Soru: İlk kural tabanlı muayene sistemleri hakkında ne söyleniyor? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Kurallar yaygın hatalarda iyi çalıştı ama yeni hata türlerinde ya da ışık ve yüzey değişimlerinde zorlandı.'

title: Fluent but Not Always Right
text:
Large language models, the systems underlying contemporary conversational assistants, are trained on vast collections of text to predict, one fragment at a time, which word is most likely to follow a given sequence. Remarkably, this seemingly modest objective, when pursued at sufficient scale, yields systems capable of summarising documents, translating between languages and writing computer code, abilities that were not explicitly programmed into them.

The same training objective, however, accounts for one of their most persistent weaknesses. Because a model is rewarded for producing plausible continuations rather than for verifying facts, it may generate statements that are fluent and confident yet false, a tendency commonly described as hallucination. A model asked for references may, for instance, supply citations to articles that do not exist, complete with credible titles and authors. Such errors are especially hazardous precisely because they are difficult to distinguish from correct output, in contrast to the obvious mistakes that earlier, less fluent systems tended to make.

Developers have pursued several countermeasures. In retrieval-augmented generation, the model is supplied with relevant passages from trusted documents and instructed to base its answer on them, thereby anchoring the output in verifiable sources. Further training with human feedback can encourage models to acknowledge uncertainty rather than guess. Nonetheless, none of these measures has eliminated the problem entirely, which is why specialists recommend that, in fields such as medicine, law or engineering, the output of such systems be treated as a draft to be checked by a qualified person rather than as an authoritative answer.

questions.q: According to the passage, language models produce hallucinations mainly because ----.
options: they are trained on too little text
they are unable to summarise documents
they were explicitly programmed to invent references with credible titles and authors
human feedback encourages them to guess
they are trained to produce plausible text rather than to check facts
questions.explain: Metin 'rewarded for producing plausible continuations rather than for verifying facts' diyor. Şık 'continuations' yerine 'text', 'verifying' yerine 'check' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Dil modelleri esas olarak neden 'halüsinasyon' üretir? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Model gerçekleri doğrulamak için değil, akla yatkın devamlar üretmek için ödüllendirilir.'

title: A Machine and Its Shadow
text:
A digital twin is a computational model of a physical asset, such as a turbine, a rolling mill or an entire factory, that is continuously updated with data from sensors on the real object, so that the virtual replica mirrors its current condition rather than merely its design. The concept is generally traced to NASA's practice, during the Apollo programme, of maintaining ground-based simulators of spacecraft, which helped engineers to devise a rescue procedure when an oxygen tank exploded aboard Apollo 13 in 1970, although the term itself became widespread only in the 2010s, once inexpensive sensors and cloud computing had made such models practicable on an industrial scale.

The principal attraction lies in predictive maintenance. Conventional maintenance is performed either at fixed intervals, which may entail replacing components that still have considerable life remaining, or after failure, which entails costly unplanned stoppages. By comparing measured vibration, temperature and load with the behaviour predicted by its model, a digital twin can flag deviations that indicate incipient wear and estimate when intervention will be necessary. It also allows operators to test changes in process parameters virtually before implementing them on the real equipment.

Nevertheless, the benefits are frequently overstated in promotional material. A twin is only as reliable as the physical understanding and data on which it rests; sensors drift, models built for one operating regime may perform poorly in another, and integrating data from equipment of different ages and manufacturers is laborious. Consequently, many so-called digital twins are, in practice, little more than dashboards displaying sensor readings, lacking the predictive model that would justify the name.

questions.q: The passage mainly ----.
options: claims that every dashboard is a genuine digital twin
argues that conventional maintenance at fixed intervals is superior to predictive maintenance

title: Seeing with Magnets
text:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) produces detailed pictures of the inside of the body without using X-rays or any other ionising radiation. It is especially good at showing soft tissues, such as the brain, muscles and ligaments, which are difficult to see clearly on ordinary X-ray images.

The method relies on the fact that the body contains a great deal of water, and every water molecule contains hydrogen nuclei, which behave like tiny magnets. When a patient lies inside the scanner, a very strong magnetic field causes many of these nuclei to line up in the same direction. Short pulses of radio waves then push them out of alignment. As the nuclei return to their original position, they give off weak radio signals, which are picked up by the machine. Because nuclei in different types of tissue return at different rates, a computer can turn these signals into images that show clear contrasts between tissues.

MRI also has some disadvantages. The scanners are expensive, and an examination can take from 15 minutes to an hour, during which the patient must stay still in a narrow tube while the machine makes loud knocking noises. Some people find this unpleasant or frightening. Moreover, because the magnet is extremely powerful and always switched on, metal objects can be pulled into the scanner at dangerous speeds, and patients with certain implants, such as some older pacemakers, may not be able to have a scan.

questions.q: According to the passage, MRI is particularly useful for ----.
options: removing metal objects from the body
producing clear images of soft tissues
showing bones more clearly than X-rays do
measuring how much water a patient drinks
treating patients with older pacemakers
questions.explain: Metin 'especially good at showing soft tissues' diyor. Şık 'especially good at showing' yerine 'particularly useful for producing clear images' kullanıyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: MRI özellikle ne için yararlı? Dayanak (1. paragraf): 'Beyin, kas ve bağ gibi yumuşak dokuları göstermede özellikle iyidir.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: metal nesneler tehlikelidir, çıkarılmaz.
Metinde kemikleri daha iyi gösterdiği yazmıyor; yumuşak doku vurgulanıyor.
Su miktarı yöntemin dayandığı bilgi; ölçülen şey değil.
Metinle çelişiyor: eski kalp pili olanlar çekim yaptıramayabilir.
questions.tip: Soruda 'particularly' varsa metinde 'especially' kelimesini ara; eş anlamlıdır.

questions.q: According to the passage, MRI can distinguish between different tissues because ----.

title: Stopping at the Tumour
text:
Conventional radiotherapy employs beams of high-energy X-rays, which deposit their dose along the entire path through the body: energy is delivered to healthy tissue in front of the tumour and, because the beam is attenuated but not stopped, to tissue behind it as well. Although modern techniques mitigate this by aiming several beams at the tumour from different angles, so that the dose is concentrated where they intersect, some irradiation of surrounding organs remains unavoidable.

Protons behave quite differently. A beam of protons deposits relatively little energy as it enters the body, but releases most of it in a narrow region near the end of its range, known as the Bragg peak, beyond which the dose falls almost to zero. By adjusting the energy of the protons, which determines how deep they penetrate, clinicians can position this peak within the tumour, thereby sparing tissue beyond it. The physicist Robert Wilson proposed the medical use of protons on this basis as early as 1946.

The advantage is most pronounced for tumours near critical structures, such as the spinal cord or the optic nerve, and for children, whose growing tissues are especially vulnerable to the long-term effects of radiation, including secondary cancers. Proton facilities, however, require a cyclotron or synchrotron and large rotating gantries, costing many times as much as a conventional unit. Furthermore, the very precision of the Bragg peak renders treatment sensitive to uncertainties in range: slight changes in patient anatomy or position may shift the peak, so that part of the tumour is missed or a healthy organ is hit. For many common cancers, randomised trials demonstrating clear superiority over advanced X-ray techniques are still awaited.

questions.q: According to the passage, the Bragg peak is ----.
options: the area of healthy tissue behind the tumour that receives the highest dose of radiation
the maximum energy that a cyclotron can produce
the narrow region near the end of a proton's range where most of its energy is released
the place where a proton beam enters the body
the point where several X-ray beams intersect
questions.explain: Metin 'releases most of it in a narrow region near the end of its range, known as the Bragg peak' diyor. Şık bunu aynen veriyor.
questions.anlam: Soru: Bragg tepesi nedir? Dayanak (2. paragraf): 'Proton ışını enerjisinin çoğunu menzilinin sonuna yakın dar bir bölgede bırakır; buna Bragg tepesi denir.'
why: Metinle çelişiyor: tepenin ötesinde doz neredeyse sıfıra iner.
Siklotronun maksimum enerjisi metinde tanımlanmıyor.
Metinle çelişiyor: giriş noktasında az enerji bırakılır.
X ışınlarının kesişmesi geleneksel radyoterapiye ait.
questions.tip: 'known as X' kalıbından önceki kısım X'in tanımıdır.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that proton therapy is considered especially suitable for children because ----.
options: children's tumours are always located near critical structures such as the spinal cord or optic nerve
protons cause more secondary cancers than X-rays

Metinle çelişiyor: proton tesisleri kat kat pahalı.
Metinle çelişiyor: anatomi değişimi risk olarak geçiyor.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a disadvantage or limitation of proton therapy?
